Overview OVERVIEW Tuesday Night Action is one US Chess-rated game every Tuesday night, completely free for CCC members. This is a great way for players to get weekly rated practice. The Top and U1600 Sections are also FIDE-rated - offering the only free weekly FIDE-rated game in the whole country. In addition, there is a free lecture before the games begin. HOW IT WORKS CCC opens Tuesdays at 5:45pm Lecture with FM Peter Giannatos prior to rated games starting at 6:00 pm Players must register weekly and in advance using the online registration system Each Tuesday evening will be limited to the first 62 players to register TNA registration will close at 6:30pm if not already full Once spots are filled, players may email events Click here to show mail address to be placed on the waitlist. ​REQUIREMENTS Players must be members of the CCC Players must have a USChess membership Open to all players in grades 9-12 and adults Students in grades K-8 must be rated over 900 K-8 players rated under 900 - See Monday Action Quads , Wednesday Action Quads , Friday Action Quads , and Sunday Action Quads ​START TIME Lecture: 6:00pm Game: 7:00pm GAMES 1 round weekly, rated at the end of the month ​ SECTIONS TOP (1600+) Under 1600 Under 1300 ​ PRIZES 2.5/3.0 score required for TNA tournaments with 3 weeks or 4.0/5.0 score required for TNA tournaments with 5 weeks. Free entries must be used for Monday Action Quads , Wednesday Action Quads , Friday Action Quads , and Sunday Action Quads within 1 month. Not transferrable to other events or players. Section winners will receive a voucher for CCC merch. TIME CONTROL Top Section: G/80, inc/10 - FIDE and US Chess Rated U1600 Section: G/60, inc/10 - FIDE and US Chess Rated U1300 Section: G/60, inc/10 - US Chess Rated ENTRY FEE Free, must be a CCC Member ​ - CCC membership only $50/year - join today !​ OTHER NOTES​​ Top and U1600 Sections are FIDE-rated - FIDE rules apply, except for US Chess penalties for cell phone infractions. Tournament Directors will accelerate pairings to pair players close in rating when possible Most recent "live" US Chess regular ratings used for all sections to ensure close matchups Open to high schoolers and adults of any rating, including unrated All players must use CCC equipment - wooden sets and digital clocks are provided PRIZES The top adult (18 or older) in each section will win a $25 gift card to USCF Sales . The top junior (under 18) in each section will win a $25 gift card to USCF Sales . All perfect scores (with perfect attendance) will receive a 3-month CCC membership extension. See special notes on site for tiebreak rules. The Charlotte Chess Center’s Main/South Location is conveniently located off of I-485 and Pineville-Matthews Road. CCC’s Main/South Branch serves both North Carolina and South Carolina. Regulars join in from Ballantyne, Pineville, SouthPark, Matthews, Mint Hill, Waxhaw, Weddington, Steele Creek, Fort Mill, Tega Cay, Rock Hill, Lake Wylie and South Charlotte. Wednesday and Friday, starting from Friday, May 1, 2020, forever Event Overview Climb the Rating Ladder Online Courses By DMV Chess since May 2020! OVERVIEW Register here: https://www.dmvchess.com/courses-register Students play one USCF-online-regular-rated game per week, after which a professional chess coach will help students analyze their games together as a group. When time permits, the coach will also give the class puzzles and lectures on tactics and strategy. Coaches are all experienced chess players who have a passion for teaching. Time control: game in 25 minutes with a 5-second increment Games submitted to the USCF for rating at the end of every month Open to scholastic players from any geographical location Wednesday class exclusively for adults Active USCF membership required Class participation strongly encouraged Groups meet online on different days for two hours . Schedule (Eastern Time): Monday class from 6:30 pm to 8:30 pm- (designed for 400 to 1000 USCF) Tuesday class from 6 pm to 8 pm- (designed for 400 to 1000 USCF) Wednesday (Adults) class from 8 pm to 10 pm- (Open) Friday class from 6 pm to 8 pm- (designed for 400 to 1000 USCF) Friday (Advanced) class from 7 pm to 9 pm- (designed for 1100 to 1600 USCF) Sunday class from 6 pm to 8 pm- (designed for 250 to 850 USCF) Coaches: Mondays: National Master Justin Burgess Tuesdays: National Master Dennis Norman Wednesdays: National Master Sam Martin Fridays: Chess Author & USCF Expert Kevin Stokker Fridays (Advanced): International Master Joshua Posthuma Sundays: USCF Expert Epiphany Peters Registration & Billing The cost of enrollment is $150/month for every course except the Friday advanced class. The cost of enrollment for the Friday Advanced course is $200/month. Fees are assessed regardless of attendance. After registering online, you will be set up for automatic monthly payments. These payments can be cancelled prior to the start of the upcoming month. To register for this course , kindly visit our website: https://www.dmvchess.com/courses-register Note: If you would like to join a class mid-month, we can send you a pro-rated invoice for the first month. By default, students who register online will be enrolled on the first of the upcoming month. After registering on the website, please email Click here to show mail address if you would like to be enrolled immediately in the middle of a month. Event Overview OVERVIEW A 3 round "quad" US Chess-rated tournament open to all adult players and youth. Quads, which group players by their skill level, are a great way to ensure closer matchups for a more fun and competitive challenge. Opportunity to play 3 regular rated games in one night! Top Quads are FIDE rapid rated! ​ WHEN Every Wednesday Night! ​ WHERE Charlotte Chess Center - Main/South Campus 10700 Kettering Drive, Unit E Charlotte, NC 28226 ​ CCC HOURS 6:00pm - 10:00pm REQUIREMENTS Participants must be members of the US Chess Federation ​ ROUND TIMES Round 1: 7:00pm Round 2: ASAP Round 3: ASAP End Time: Between 8:30pm-10:00pm depending on quad. HOW IT WORKS Players must register weekly and in advance Quads - players placed into groups of 4 by their most recent US Chess rating* 3 US Chess rated games every Wednesday night Top 6 quads also FIDE rapid rated Each evening will be limited to the first 60 players to register Entries are first registered, first served​ *Minor roster shifts to avoid family member pairings may be possible ​​ PRIZES $40 to the winner(s) of each quad; $45 for perfect 3-0 score TIME CONTROL G/20; Increment 10 Each player receives 20 minutes plus a 10 second bonus each move to complete each game ENTRY FEE CCC Members Rated 2000+: Free Entry ( $20 deducted from any prize ) CCC Members: $20.00 Non-Members: $25.00 ​ Join the CCC and Save - Only $50 a Year - Save on Camps, Classes, Tournaments and More! Rochester Chess Center weekly on Wednesday, starting from Wednesday, January 4, 2023, forever Event Overview 1 USCF-Rated Game, G/80 d5. New players welcome. *EF: $6 for visiting players; CCCR members $4. Register on-site: 6:30-7:15 pm. Rd.: 7:30pm. *US Chess Membership is required and can be done on-site during registration. Cost varies by age group: 20 (Youth), $27 Young Adult, $45 Adult, $40 Senior. Details for eligibility for each age group is available from the US Chess site and during registration at the Chess Center. Snack bar on-site at the Chess Center. Many special events take place throughout the year including our annual club championship. Club Membership is optional. Club membership is $30 for individual members and $40 for family members in same household. Chess game pairing is generally arranged by closest chess rating available. New players generally play the lower-rated players. Our Club's Web Site: www.rochesterchessclub.org Rochester Chess Center store on-site for all your chess needs, including sets, boards, clocks, books and more. You may schedule Chess Lessons and Sign-up for Chess Camps run by the Rochester Chess Center. History: Our chess club has been hosting chess players for over 60 years. During this time, thousands of USCF-rated chess games have been played, and countless unrated chess games have been played (e.g. Blitz, Simultaneous exhibitions, etc.). Weekly club meetings are held at the Rochester Chess Center located at 221 Norris Drive, Rochester, NY 14610; Phone: (585) 442-2430. We welcome all chess players & curious visitors. Currently, we have chess players of all ages with USCF ratings from beginner to Master strength. All are welcome. Club Organization: Club President: Ken McBride (Local TD), Vice President: Jamshed Ahmed (Club TD), Treasurer/Organizer: Mike Lionti (Senior TD), Club Secretary: Mike Runnells, Club Officers: Mike Runnells and David Worl. Several other TDs and volunteers also assist us. Event Overview DKC Grand Prix Tournament Information September 2023 Dragon Knight Chess Grand Prix Tournaments Join us for chess tournaments in our new home at 2000 Bearcat Way, Suite 104, Morrisville 27560 , where we are hosting our September tournaments Friday-Sunday (plus a special Labor Day tournament)! Players of all ages and experience levels are invited to attend. Entry fee: $20 in advance, or $30 onsite. Entry fees help to fund the 2023 Dragon Knight Chess ("DKC") Grand Prix. Time controls: Saturday and Sunday afternoons (1pm) : Time control for sections below 800: Game in 25 minutes; 5 second delay/move. Time control for sections above 800; Game in 45 minutes; 5 second delay/move Time control for Friday night (6pm) Quick : Game in 15 minutes; 5 second delay/move Cash prizes in the top rated section: 1st: $40 2nd: $27 3rd: $13 New scholastic tournament players receive a 1 year USCF membership! New players are welcome! Sections have 4 players each by rating (Quad Setup). Below the top rated section, 1st place wins a trophy, 2nd place wins a medal, and 3rd place wins a small scorebook. (Alternative prizes are available.) Also, all players who adequately record the moves in their tournament games get a keychain chess piece. Adults are invited to participate, but must have a US Chess Federation Membership which can be purchased here: https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess Free Blitz Tourna ments! Free blitz tournaments are scheduled immediately following the regular Saturday and Sunday afternoon tournaments. These are recommended for all adults ages 16 and up; and for players younger than 16 with ratings of at least 700. Double Round Robin, or Swiss System if many entries Time control is Game in 5 minutes; +2 second increment each move Blitz tournament starts on Saturday and Sundays at 4:30pm (or immediately after players complete 1pm tournament) Estimated end: 7pm Free blitz! No immediate cash prizes, but points count toward the 2023 Dragon Knight Chess Grand Prix! USCF rated - Adult players must have current USCF membership Rated DKC tournament points scored earn 2023 DKC Grand Prix points, which earn prizes for category winners. North Charlotte Chess Center (North) weekly on Friday, starting from Friday, May 3, 2024, forever Event Overview Friday Action Quads - North A three round US Chess-rated tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads, which group students in sections of 4 by their rating level, are a great way for students to get closer matchups for a more fun and competitive challenge. During the Fall and Spring seasons, this event does count for eligibility towards the Tournament of Champions . ​ CHECK OUT ALL OF OUR EVENTS! WHEN Every Friday Night! Can't make Friday evenings? Great alternatives are: Sunday Action Quads ( CCC Main/South ) Monday Action Quads ( CCC North ) Friday Action Quads is also offered at our South Location - Info Here REGISTRATION Limited to first 42 to register. Registration must be completed online ahead of the event. REQUIREMENTS Ages 17 and under Participants must be members of the US Chess Federation US Chess is the governing body of chess in the US and conducts all of the rating calculations for players. Need a US Chess Membership? Purchase through the CCC and save ! ​​ ROUND TIMES Round 1: 7:00pm Round 2: ASAP Round 3: ASAP Approximate End Time: 9:00pm HOW IT WORKS Players must register weekly and in advance 3 US Chess regular and quick rated games every Friday night Quad format - students placed into groups of 4 by their most current "live" US Chess regular rating to ensure closer matchups. Each evening will be limited to the first 42 players to register Entries are first registered, first served Quads are for students (K-12) only​ PRIZES Medal to winner of each quad ​​ TIME CONTROL G/20; Increment 10 Each player receives 20 minutes plus a 10 second bonus each move to complete each game ​ ENTRY FEE Players currently rated 1500+: FREE Entry (see special notes for details) CCC Members: $17.50 Non-Members: $22.50 ​ Join the CCC and Save - Only $50 a Year - Save on Camps, Classes, Tournaments and more! The Charlotte Chess Center’s North Branch is conveniently located off of I-485 and Benfield Road. Opened in September of 2023, the CCC’s North Branch serves North Charlotte, University City, Concord, Kannapolis, Harrisburg, Huntersville, Cornelius, Davidson, Lake Norman, and Mooresville. Regulars visit from both North Carolina and South Carolina. **Presented by Implodians Chess School LLC** Join us for an exciting day of competitive chess at the Novi's AccelerateKid Scholastic Tournament, sponsored by The Implodians Chess School LLC. This event is designed to provide young chess enthusiasts with a platform to showcase their skills, challenge themselves, and enjoy the spirit of competition. **Date and Time:** May 19th, starting at 10:00 AM EASTERN( this week only ,then back to every 2nd sunday) **Venue:** 24404 Catherine Industrial Dr #316, Novi, MI 48377 **Tournament Format:** - 5 Round Swiss - USCF REGULAR Rated - 3 Sections: Open, Under 900, Under 600 - Time Control: G/30; d5 (5-second delay) **Entry Fee:** $30 per participant. Ensure your spot by registering before the deadline on April 13th at 9:00 PM. **Tournament Schedule:** - Rounds begin at 10am, followed by 11:15am, 1:00pm, 2:15pm, and 3:30pm. - Pairings for each round will be created as soon as possible after the previous round ends. - The tournament is anticipated to conclude before 5pm. **Awards:** - Trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd places in the Open and Under 900 sections. - In the Under 600 section, trophies will be awarded to the top 5 finishers (1st through 5th). - A special "Best Notation Award" will be given to the participant with the most legible and accurate score sheet. - All awards are based on a minimum of 50 entries. **Registration:** Secure your participation by registering online at [https://onlineregistration.cc/](https://onlineregistration.cc/). Don't miss the chance to be part of this enriching chess experience! **Contact Information:** For more details about the tournament, please reach out to Bryan Wilson at (313)878-2807 or via email at [ [email protected] ](mailto: [email protected] ). This tournament promises to be a day filled with strategic thinking, sportsmanship, and fun. Whether you're a seasoned player or new to the world of competitive chess, the Novi's AccelerateKid Scholastic Tournament is the perfect opportunity to improve your game, meet fellow chess enthusiasts, and possibly take home a trophy. Register now and be part of this exciting chess event! Players currently rated 1200+: Free Entry Free Entry Policy: Free entry is offered to scholastic (K-12) players who have a current "live Over The Board (OTB)" US Chess rating of 1200+. No exceptions. To get free entry, players must register online mid-day before the event (Noon Saturday). If you register for free but must cancel, email [email protected] or text (919) 422-2535 by 9:00am (one hour before Round 1 of the quad). Players receiving free entry are not permitted to withdraw mid-quad, without permission from all other players in their quad. Free entry players who withdraw mid-quad (without permission) will not be eligible for free entry in future Dragon Knight Chess quads. US Chess membership required; Dragon Knight Chess will use vouchers to create new scholastic memberships. US Chess is the governing body of chess in the United States. US Chess conducts all rating calculations for players. Time Control: Above USCF 800 sections G/40; delay 5 (3 games): Each player receives 40 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. USCF U800 sections G/25; delay 5 (3-6 games): Each player receives 25 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. Onsite registration 9:00-9:30am day of tournament. Round Times: 1st Round 10:00am; Round 2: ASAP; Round 3: ASAP End Time: Between Noon-1pm, depending on quad. How it Works: Players must register weekly. Quads: Players are placed into groups of 4 by their most recent "live" US Chess regular rating. (Minor section shifts are possible, to avoid family member pairings.) 3-6 rated games each Sunday morning Each Sunday morning is limited to the first 40 players to register. Entries are first registered, first served. Quads are for K-12 students only. Kennedy Recreation & Aquatic Center. weekly on Tuesday and Friday, starting from Tuesday, September 24, 2024, forever Event Overview Unlock Your Chess Potential at Newark JFK Recreation! Are you ready to dive into the exciting world of chess? Newark JFK Recreation is thrilled to announce our comprehensive chess program, catering to players from beginners to advanced levels! Join us every Tuesday and Friday from 4:30 PM to 6 PM for engaging lessons and strategic gameplay that will elevate your skills. What We Offer: Beginner to Advanced Classes : Whether you’re just starting out or looking to sharpen your tactics, our skilled instructors will guide you through the intricacies of the game. You'll learn essential techniques, openings, and strategies to outsmart your opponents. Introduction to Tournament Play : Immediately following our classes, we will introduce you to the thrilling world of tournament play. Discover what it takes to compete, and gain valuable insights into the competitive chess landscape. Opportunity to Represent Our Club : We’re excited to announce that the chess club will be selecting players to represent us in upcoming team tournaments! This is your chance to showcase your skills, gain experience, and be part of a passionate community of chess enthusiasts. Why Join Us? Chess is more than just a game; it’s a fantastic way to develop critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and patience. Plus, it’s a great way to make new friends and become part of a supportive community. Whether you’re playing for fun or aspiring to compete, there’s a place for you here. How to Get Involved: Don’t miss out on this fantastic opportunity to enhance your chess skills and join our vibrant chess community! Simply come to Newark JFK Recreation on Tuesdays or Fridays at 4:30 PM, and we’ll take care of the rest. Bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn, and let’s make some moves together! We look forward to seeing you on the board! Let’s checkmate those challenges and have fun along the way. For more information, feel free to reach out to us or visit our website. Happy playing! ♟️ Address: 211 W. tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads group players by their skill level. This is a chance to play 3-6 rated (regular and quick) games each Sunday afternoon! New School Montessori Center 5617 Sunset Lake Road Holly Springs, NC 27540 (919) 422-2535 3-6 round (Single or Double) Quad Round Robin sections First place trophy in each 4 player section. Team trophy to top school overall. Other prizes will also be awarded. Registration and Entry Fee: $19 online mid-day before the event (Noon Saturday), or $29 onsite registration 12:30-1pm day of tournament. Players currently rated 1200+: Free Entry Free Entry Policy: Free entry is offered to scholastic (K-12) players who have a current "live Over The Board (OTB)" US Chess rating of 1200+. No exceptions. To get free entry, players must register online mid-day before the event (Noon Saturday). If you register for free but must cancel, email [email protected] or text (919) 422-2535 by 12:30pm (one hour before Round 1 of the quad). Players receiving free entry are not permitted to withdraw mid-quad, without permission from all other players in their quad. Free entry players who withdraw mid-quad (without permission) will not be eligible for free entry in future Dragon Knight Chess quads. US Chess membership required; Dragon Knight Chess will use vouchers to create new scholastic memberships. US Chess is the governing body of chess in the United States. US Chess conducts all rating calculations for players. Time Control: Above USCF 800 sections G/40; delay 5 (3 games): Each player receives 40 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. USCF U800 sections G/24; delay 4 (3-6 games): Each player receives 24 minutes (plus a 4 second delay each move) to complete each game. Onsite registration 12:30-1pm day of tournament. Round Times: 1st Round 1:30pm; Round 2: ASAP; Round 3: ASAP End Time: Between 3-4:30pm, depending on quad. How it Works: Players must register weekly. Quads: Players are placed into groups of 4 by their most recent "live" US Chess rating. (Minor section shifts are possible, to avoid family member pairings.) 3-6 rated games each Sunday afternoon Each Sunday afternoon is limited to the first 50 players to register. Entries are first registered, first served. Quads are for K-12 students only. time control of G/30;d5. The event is held at the Texas Chess Center in Irving: 4343 W Royal Ln STE 114, Irving, TX 75063. General expected schedule (subject to slight variation): Registration ends: 1:45pm Round 1 pairings posted: 2:00pm Opening announcements: 2:05pm Round 1 begins: 2:10pm Subsequent rounds: ASAP after the completion of the prior round Latest expected end-time of last game (most will end far earlier): 7:10pm After Round 1, subsequent rounds are conducted on an ASAP basis, with midround transitions being employed as often as appropriate. All necessary equipment (clocks, boards, pieces, notation sheets, and pencils) will be supplied for you. There are three sections, into which entrants are automatically placed (based on their latest Monthly US Chess rating): Championship U1000 U600 Players whose Monthly ratings are within 150 points of the section cap may, for a $10 fee, request to play up one section. Approval of this request is subject to the organizers' discretion. Masters (NM+) enjoy free entry, with no deduction from any prizes won. Prizes (all guaranteed): Championship: Cash prizes for 1st and 2nd 1st place receives 20% of total Championship section entry fees 2nd place receives 10% of total Championship section entry fees Minimum prizes are $50 for 1st, $25 for 2nd U1000: Trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd U600: Medals for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Address: 4343 West Royal Lane STE 114 Irving , TX 75063 United States Sections: 3 Grand Prix Points: Prize Fund: FIDE Rated: No Handicap Accessible: No Residency Restriction: No Online Event: No Organizer Overview Texas Chess Center Email: [email protected] Phone: 469-900-8014 Website: https://www.texaschesscenter.com/ Footer About US Chess Privacy Policy Terms of Use Mission & Vision Governance Annual Reports Delegates List Information for Delegates Registered Voters Committees Advertise Media Kit Staff/Contact Us Board Requests for Proposals (RFP) Join Membership Terms and Conditions Redeem a Voucher Benefactor Members Give Donate Online World Youth Championship US Olympiad Team At-Risk Youth Footer Play Safe Play Policy New to Chess? month-long tournament with one US Chess-rated game every Wednesday. The tournament is an excellent opportunity for players of all ages and skill levels to participate in weekly rated practice. With classical time controls, players can take their time to think more thoroughly about their moves and strengthen their calculation skills. Details: Schedule : Rounds start weekly at 7 pm; Format: 1 round per week. Games are submitted for rating at the end of the month; 4 rounds/month (5 rounds in some months) Time Control: 30moves/90minutes + sudden death 30minutes, both time controls have 5-second delay starting move one Sections: one open section Players must have an active US Chess membership. Saturday, starting from Saturday, August 16, 2025, forever Event Overview UPDATE: There will be no tournament on Saturday, Jan. 31, due to inclement weather. Tournaments resume Saturday, Feb. 7. Each Saturday at 1:30pm A 3-6 round "quad" US Chess rated tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads group players by their skill level. This is a chance to play 3-6 rated (regular and quick) games each Saturday afternoon! Dragon Knight Chess Center 2000 Bearcat Way Suite 104 Morrisville, NC 27560 (919) 422-2535 3-6 round (Single or Double) Quad Round Robin sections First place trophy in each 4 player section. Team trophy to top school overall. Other prizes will also be awarded. Registration and Entry Fee: $19 online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday), or $29 onsite registration 12:30-1pm day of tournament. Players currently rated 1200+: Free Entry Free Entry Policy: Free entry is offered to scholastic (K-12) players who have a current "live Over The Board (OTB)" US Chess rating of 1200+. No exceptions. To get free entry, players must register online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday). If you register for free but must cancel, email [email protected] or text (919) 422-2535 by 12:30pm (one hour before Round 1 of the quad). Players receiving free entry are not permitted to withdraw mid-quad, without permission from all other players in their quad. Free entry players who withdraw mid-quad (without permission) will not be eligible for free entry in future Dragon Knight Chess quads. US Chess membership required; Dragon Knight Chess will use vouchers to create new scholastic memberships. US Chess is the governing body of chess in the United States. US Chess conducts all rating calculations for players. Time Control: Above USCF 800 sections G/40; delay 5 (3 games): Each player receives 40 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. USCF U800 sections G/25; delay 5 (3-6 games): Each player receives 25 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. Onsite registration 12:30-1pm day of tournament. Round Times: 1st Round 1:30pm; Round 2: ASAP; Round 3: ASAP End Time: Between 3-4pm, depending on quad. How it Works: Players must register weekly. Quads: Players are placed into groups of 4 by their most recent "live" US Chess rating. (Minor section shifts are possible, to avoid family member pairings.) 3-6 rated games each Saturday afternoon Each Saturday afternoon is limited to the first 50 players to register. Entries are first registered, first served. Quads are for K-12 students only. IMPROVE - Game analysis and blitz with Dragon Knight Chess coaches IM Jonathan Schroer and Paul Ascolese (peak FIDE rating 2275) SIDE EVENTS - Free USCF rated blitz tournaments start as early as 1:30pm. For questions, concerns, and withdrawals prior to the event email: [email protected] For contact during the event email (above) or text (or call) ( 919) 422-2535 Handicap Accessible NO Residency Restriction: Open to all scholastic players! Saturday, starting from Saturday, October 11, 2025, forever Event Overview Each Saturday at 10am A 3-6 round "quad" US Chess rated tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads group players by their skill level. This is a chance to play 3-6 rated (regular and quick) games each Saturday morning! Dragon Knight Chess Center 2000 Bearcat Way Suite 104 Morrisville, NC 27560 (919) 422-2535 3-6 round (Single or Double) Quad Round Robin sections First place trophy in each 4 player section. Team trophy to top school overall. Other prizes will also be awarded. Registration and Entry Fee: $19 online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday), or $29 onsite registration 9-9:30am day of tournament. Players currently rated 1200+: Free Entry Free Entry Policy: Free entry is offered to scholastic (K-12) players who have a current "live Over The Board (OTB)" US Chess rating of 1200+. No exceptions. To get free entry, players must register online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday). If you register for free but must cancel, email [email protected] or text (919) 422-2535 by 9am (one hour before Round 1 of the quad). Players receiving free entry are not permitted to withdraw mid-quad, without permission from all other players in their quad. Free entry players who withdraw mid-quad (without permission) will not be eligible for free entry in future Dragon Knight Chess quads. US Chess membership required; Dragon Knight Chess will use vouchers to create new scholastic memberships. US Chess is the governing body of chess in the United States. US Chess conducts all rating calculations for players. Time Control: Above USCF 800 sections G/40; delay 5 (3 games): Each player receives 40 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. USCF U800 sections G/25; delay 5 (3-6 games): Each player receives 25 minutes (plus a 5 second delay each move) to complete each game. Onsite registration 9-9:30am day of tournament. Round Times: 1st Round 10am; Round 2: ASAP; Round 3: ASAP End Time: Between Noon-1pm, depending on quad. How it Works: Players must register weekly. Quads: Players are placed into groups of 4 by their most recent "live" US Chess rating. (Minor section shifts are possible, to avoid family member pairings.) 3-6 rated games each Saturday morning Each Saturday morning is limited to the first 50 players to register. between 6:00-8:45 pm (on-site registration between 5:30-5: 55 pm). Adults, kids and all levels of players are welcome. SPACE IS LIMITED TO THE FIRST 60 REGISTRANTS. PLEASE REGISTER BEFORE 5:45 PM. NO LATE REGISTRATION IS ALLOWED. Time control: G/25; d5 (3 Rounds; USCF dual-rated) Sections: The tournament has four sections: Advanced Section: USCF rating >=1400 USCF Championship Section: USCF rating 1000-1399 USCF Reserve section: USCF 600-999 USCF. Beginner section: USCF Under 600 USCF. TD reserves the right to revise section breaks or provide wild cards. Byes are allowed in any round as long as you let us know by at least 1 round in advance. Entry fees: $5 per tournament. We accept online payment or credit card on-site. No Cash Transactions. Online registration is highly preferred. WWW.TOURNAMENTSIGNUP.COM . Please enter your complete name and USCF ID when you register. PLEASE REGISTER BEFORE 5:45 PM. NO LATE REGISTRATION IS ALLOWED. Mandatory requirement: Please bring a valid USCF membership ID number for registration. Additional details at http://chesscardinals.com on how to apply online for USCF membership. Our team can help you get a membership on-site too. Optional requirement: Notation is optional. Notation books are available for purchase on-site. Grand Prix Prizes: Based on all the “Thursday tournaments” in a month, we will tally up points and give trophies to reward improvement in chess skill and encourage participation. For each night’s attendance, you get 3 points for showing up, and for each Win 1 point, each Draw or 1/2-Byes 0.5 point (we will use the USCF cross-table for the event). Regardless of which sections you played, prizes include Top Prize 1st (Champions Trophy). Additional prizes may be awarded depending on the available funds. SIGNS: Look for the Chess Cardinals banner. Restrooms: Ground floor near emergency EXIT. Separate for MEN/WOMEN. You would need keys. Please RESTROOM KEYS sign on the wall to locate these keys. The Santa Paula Oddfellows Lodge # 314 weekly on Wednesday, starting from Wednesday, October 29, 2025, forever Event Overview THE CHESS RUN WEDNESDAYS is a month-long tournament with one US Chess-rated game every Wednesday. The tournament is an excellent opportunity for players of all ages and skill levels to participate in weekly rated practice. With classical time controls, players can take their time to think more thoroughly about their moves and strengthen their calculation skills. Event Overview FIRST SATURDAY ONLINE GRAND PRIX Join our monthly online tournament series - designed for all K-12 chess players who love to compete, learn and grow! Overview The First Saturday Online Grand Prix is a seven-tournament scholastic series open to all K-12 students nationwide. Each monthly event offers its own prize and also counts toward the overall Grand Prix leaderboard. Players may join any number of tournaments. Schedule Platform : lichess.org Time control : G/15; +5 seconds increment Start Time : 10 AM EST Format : 4 rounds Swiss Dates : November 1, 2025; December 6, 2025; January 3, 2026; February 7, 2026; March 7, 2026; April 4, 2026; May 2 2026. Entry fee : $20 Prizes 1st place winner of each tournament: One free private online lesson with WFM Bahar Hallayeva (An exclusive opportunity to learn directly from a titled chess master!) Grand Prix Points and Series Awards Players earn Grand Prix points in each tournament. Cumulative points across all seven events determine the Overall Grand Prix Winners: 1st place: Trophy + 3 months of Chess for Everyone weekly online classes ($300 value) 2nd place: Trophy + 2 months of Chess for Everyone weekly online classes ($200 value) 3rd place: Trophy + 1 month of Chess for Everyone weekly online classes ($100 value) Eligibility Open to all K-12 students Players may join any number of tournaments to qualify for Grand Prix prizes This tournament will be USCF online quick rated. An active USCF membership is required. You can join the USCF or renew an expired USCF membership at this link: http://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess . You can choose 1 or 2 years plan. Before signing up for the tournament, please register for a free https://lichess.org account. Please provide your lichess username in the "Lichess username" field when you complete the registration form. Fair Play Policy Games are played on lichess.org No outside assistance or chess engines allowed Violations may lead to disqualification After you register, you will receive an email from us with instructions on how to join the tournament online. At-Risk-Youth Seniors Women menu arrow_back TUESDAY CHESS NIGHT (3ss, 25+5) by Indy Chess Latvian Community Center weekly on Tuesday, starting from Tuesday, January 6, 2026, forever Event Overview All are welcome to join us for Indy's largest weekly chess night at the Latvian Community Center! Register ahead of time at indychess.org/events! There are three areas in which you can play chess: 1) USCF-RATED TOURNAMENT ROOM There's a 3-round, Swiss system, G/25+5 USCF-rated tournament (typically two or three sections determined by rating) in a separate room from about 6:30pm to 9:30pm. Arrive by 6:15pm if you want to be paired in round one (if you are a regular and you pre-register online, just text Mike if you can't arrive by 6:15pm so we know to pair you and start the clock). Games affect both USCF regular and quick ratings. Must be a member of USCF to play rated chess (new.uschess.org/join-us-chess). Make sure to provide your USCF ID# to [email protected] prior to the event, or arrive by 6:15pm to be paired in round one. First visit = free (but arrive by 6:15p)! Other visits are $5 members/$10 non-members (club membership is $50/yr). 2) KIDS' WORKSHOP AND QUADS There will be a kids' game review workshop from 6:30-7:00, followed by kids casual play from 7:00-8:00pm. Kids can earn medals, and eventually cash in medals for trophies. Kids typically play in "quads" after the lesson, meaning we place them in groups of four according to their level and they play each kid in the quad one time! First Tuesday of each month we play "Bughouse" (two-on-two chess). Participation in the kids' area costs $5 (members) / $10 (non-members), but the first visit is free (just show up). Pay at the door by 6:30p, or save time and register in advance at indychess.org/events. Parents are requested to stay the first visit, but future visits can leave and return by 7:50pm. 3) ADULT CASUAL Adult casual play (13+ years old) will also be available 6:30-9:30pm, so come make some friends and meet new opponents. Adults pair themselves for pick-up games. Sets and clocks are provided (you can bring your own as well), and any time control is allowed as you desire. Adult Casual section is always free; just show up and play pick-up games! The rooms are wheelchair accessible. All chess equipment is provided (though feel free to bring your own). There is a cash-only drinks vending machine, but many players bring a water bottle as the water fountain is broken. Register for chess night at indychess.org/events! Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . Hope to see you there! Overview ICEA Chess @ West LA hosts a Monthly OTB Chess Tournament on the second Saturday of each month. It typically features four sections (U1000, 1000+, 1600+ and 2000+) to accommodate different skill levels based on the monthly supplement USCF ratings. The tournament is a one-day event with four rounds for the 1000+ / 1600+ / 2000+ sections, running from 9 AM to 6 PM, with a time control of G/45;+5 (45 minutes for each player, plus a 5-second increment per move). The U1000 section is designed for players with ratings below 1000, making it an excellent starting point for new players who haven't established a USCF rating yet. This section has three double rounds from 9 AM to 4 PM, meaning players will play two games against the same opponent each round. Weekly Blitz Tournament , where quick thinking and sharp instincts matter most. This USCF-rated event features six single round of nonstop action, with a time control of G/3 +2 , ensuring every game is intense from the first move to the last. Open to players of all skill levels , the tournament offers a competitive yet welcoming environment—perfect for seasoned blitz specialists and players looking to sharpen their speed-chess skills. All USCF rules apply , and a current USCF membership is required . Half-point byes (maximum of two) are available upon request and must be submitted before the end of Round 1. Whether you’re chasing rating points, testing new ideas, or simply enjoying fast-paced chess with fellow enthusiasts, our weekly blitz promises exciting games, great competition, and a lively chess atmosphere. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or drinks in waiting area while games are in progress. -Boards and clocks will be provided. -By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well. ♟️♟️♟️ For questions: Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890 ♟️♟️♟️ Tournament Director: Mariela Trevino ♟️♟️♟️ ♟️♟️♟️ Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette: Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute. Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible. One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock. Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. You will have 15 minutes plus a 2 second delay in each turn. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically. Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent). Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand. "J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it. Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square. No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play. Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be curteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen. Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe. Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent. Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section. Games start at 8pm, but if both opponents want to start sooner when pairings are ready (hopefully by 7:30pm) that's okay too! Entry Fees Prize Pool (For folks who want to win prize money; byes must be declared on first played round, one half point bye ok) $80 for Social and Non Members $60 for Full and Family Members No-Prize (For folks who want to play stronger players but don't mind not being able to win prizes; half point byes are available any round) $30 for Social and Non Members $25 for Full and Family Members Per-game, No-Prize (This is for folks with uncertain schedules, visiting players, etc., all rounds un-played are half point byes for pairing purposes.) $15 per game for Social and Non Members $10 per game for Full and Family Members Prizes(80%!!): Prizes are determined by the total number of entries, prize players and non-prize players. Seniors Women menu arrow_back ACC Friday Online Blitz Albany Chess Center Team on lichess.org weekly on Friday, starting from Friday, February 6, 2026, 8 times Event Overview Albany Chess Center Online Blitz is a weekly 9-round Swiss tournament held on the Albany Chess Center Team on lichess.org. Rounds are played every Friday from 6:00 pm to 8:00 pm Eastern Time. The time control is 3 minutes with a 2-second increment (3+2) for each game. Pairings and results are handled automatically by lichess, and players should join the Albany Chess Center team page in advance to participate. There is a 25 dollar gift card awarded each month to the best overall performer across that month’s Friday events; tie-breaks, eligibility, and fair-play decisions are at the discretion of the tournament director. Before signing up for the tournament, please register for a lichess.org account (it's free!) if you do not have an existing account. If you have any issues try watching this"> video we originally made for our scholastic tournaments about how to register an account on lichess: XTr_tAh7JeQ"> There will be two sections: Open and Under 1300 . These sections are determined by over-the-board USCF-regular rating. For example, a player with a rating of 1350 would belong in the Open section, a player rated 1200 would belong in the Under 1300 section, and so forth. Unrated players can play in any section. If you don't know which section you belong in, feel free to contact us. All participants must be active members of the US Chess Federation. Players can withdraw from the event at any time by pressing the "withdraw" button. Prizes : Plaques for 1st, and trophies for 2nd and 3rd in both sections. All plaques and trophies will be inscribed with the winner's name. Tiebreaks are calculated based on the Sonneborn–Berger method, after which we use lichess performance ratings as a secondary tiebreak. 1st-place trophies are always awarded to players with a perfect score, even in the event of a tie. If you live outside of the contiguous United States, we might not be able to mail your trophy due to the increased shipping costs for international orders (or we may ask the foreign player to pay a shipping fee). After you register, you will receive an email from us with instructions on how to join the tournament online. If you don't receive the email, please check your spam folder by typing the word instructions into your spam or junk folder. We encourage players to complete the registration process and join the tournament online before 1:45 pm ET. If you're late to the tournament you could end up missing round 1! Players will not be required to join a Zoom call during the tournament, but we will monitor the games very closely to ensure fair play. Lichess has an excellent algorithm for detecting cheating, and we will also do a post-tournament fair-play inspection. If a participant's account is flagged for cheating by lichess, we have the prerogative to submit the player's games as losses for USCF-rating purposes, or (in rare cases) annul the games. Southpark Friday, February 20, 2026 - Sunday, February 22, 2026 Event Overview https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/febopen OVERVIEW The Charlotte February Open is a classical event with a $6,000 guaranteed total prize fund - $5,500 in the main event plus a free $500 Saturday evening blitz tournament. All sections are US Chess and FIDE rated. There is a minimum rating of 1200 and registration cap of 140 players. WHEN February 20-22, 2026 3-day and 2-day schedules available ​ WHERE Beautiful Venue in the Heart of Southpark! Walk to Starbucks, Whole Foods and more! Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark 4808 Sharon Road Charlotte, NC 28210 (704) 362-5080 Free internet, free parking ​ ​ HOTEL BOOKING Both hotel options attached to the playing venue. Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark $134/night for King or $149 for 2 Queens Booking Link - Reserve ASAP Homewood Suites - Southpark $152/night for King suite with sofa bed Booking Link - Reserve ASAP ELIGIBILITY There is a strict minimum rating of 1200 to enter, based on February US Chess ratings or a peak rating achieved between January 1 - February 20. See events schedule for other options this weekend. Registration Cap: 140 players. The organizer may continue to accept registration past 140 players based on specific space constraints. REGISTRATION Online registration only - no on-site registration. All registration closes 90 minutes before round 1 start time. On-site check-in is not necessary . TIME CONTROLS 3-Day Schedule: G/110; inc/10 Rounds 1-2 of 2-day: G/30, inc/10 PRIZES & SECTIONS $5,500 Guaranteed Prize Fund in 3 Sections . Championship Section - FIDE Rated $1000 – $700 – $400 Top U2200: $400 40 US Chess Grand Prix Points ​ Under 2000 Section - FIDE Rated $700 – $400 – $200 Top U1800: $300 Under 1600 Section - FIDE Rated $600 – $300 – $200 Top U1400: $300 Minimum rating of 1200. 100-point Rule applies for "playing up" - see Special Notes below. Plaques to first place in all sections. SCHEDULE 3-Day Schedule - 5 Rounds Friday: 6:30pm Saturday: 10:30am & 4:00pm Sunday: 10:00am & 3:00pm ​ 2-Day Schedule - 5 Rounds Saturday: 10:30am*, 1:00pm*, 4:00pm Sunday: 10:00am & 3:00pm ​ * Rounds 1-2 of 2-Day Schedule played at G/30; inc/10 time control, then merge with 3-day schedule, Saturday 4:00pm FREE FEBRUARY OPEN BLITZ Saturday 8:45pm Blitz Registration On-site only, Saturday 4:00-8:30pm No online or emailed blitz registration Free blitz entry for players in the February Open Open to all players - $30 on-site blitz entry for those not in the February Open 6 (single) Rounds – US Chess regular ratings used for pairings/prizes. US Chess and FIDE blitz rated. US Chess membership required. $500 guaranteed prize fund in one section: $200 - $100 - $60. Top U2000: $80, Top U1700: $60. ENTRY FEE $135 by February 9 $150 after February 9 GM/IM/WGMs : Free online entry, no deduction from prize if registered by January 20, otherwise $135 deducted from prize. Re-entry: $60. See information under "Special Notes" below. Sunday, February 22, 2026 Event Overview Take your game to the next level with BayAreaChess REAL-FIDE tournaments — tailored for players seeking FIDE ratings and serious competition! Whether you're chasing norms or climbing the international ladder, the BayAreaChess REAL-FIDE offers a professional chess environment, perfect for ambitious scholastic and adult players alike. Register here You must log in or sign up before you can register. Online registration closes at 12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament. Onsite registration is subject to availability (additional fee incurred). Late fee ($30) applied on February 19 or when reaching capacity. Schedule 2 schedules available ( More info ) 3-day option: Rounds: 6 Time Control: 6x G/90 +30 Round Times: ‣ Fri, Feb. 20 - 6:30 p.m. ‣ Sat, Feb. 21 - 9:30 a.m., 1:50 p.m., 6:10 p.m. ‣ Sun, Feb. 22 - 9:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m. 2-day option: Rounds: 6 Time Controls: 2x G/55 d5, 4x G/90 +30 Round Times: ‣ Sat, Feb. 21 - 9:00 a.m., 11:20 a.m., 1:50 p.m., 6:10 p.m. ‣ Sun, Feb. 22 - 9:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m. ½-point byes are available for any round (Max byes: 3; byes must be requested at least 30 min before that round's start except last round byes; last round bye must be requested latest before Round 3) 0-point byes are available for any round (player must play at least half the rounds to be eligible for prizes) Sections Players will be placed into one of the three sections based on February 2026 Published Supplement rating: Open (1800+) FIDE-rated AB (1400-1799) FIDE-rated CDEu (unr. & u1400) A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is NOT allowed. Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up, and within 200 points in highest section. (Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their February 2026 Published Supplement rating.) Prizes Prize Fund: $4,000 Guaranteed! ( More info ) Regular entry winners get full prize, Econ entry winners get 50% prize. Unrated winners: Max $200 (except in the top section) A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for prize money. Prizes will be paid out by check (mail), PayPal or Zelle. Fees Regular entry: $148 Econ entry: $111 Play up fee: +$28 Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ) Onsite fee: +$33 (membership discounts are not redeemable onsite) Withdrawals Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to a 4% processing fee. Only withdrawals made before the tournament day are eligible for refund. Change requests After registration, changes can be requested at bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees: until Feb. 18, $7 change fee. on Feb. 19, $15 change fee. The following requests are exempt from the change fee: playing up to a higher section. requesting byes. Other requirements USCF membership must be active. More information available here . Minimum four players or section will be merged with lower section. Prize eligibility remains the same; all prizes guaranteed. Playing up sections is not allowed by request. Playing down one section by request is allowed. Tournament Director has full discretion with pairings and moving players into different sections if necessary. Why play a six-hour game when you can play a one-hour game for the same rating points? With modern computer analysis, chess growth happens away from the board, reviewing played games. FOUR COMPLETE GAMES in the same time of one traditional tournament game means FOUR times the learning opportunity and FOUR times the potential rating point gain - all in one evening. Action Chess is the most competitive and most fun form of standard-rated chess! If you're trying to become an Expert, Master, or scholastic player trying to move up the age lists, Action Chess is your best way to achieve your goals. This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address ! Three players in the rated sections attending the same school (as of the spring 2026 semester). Teams have no upper limit; the more players on a team, the higher the chances for a good result, but only the top 3 players’ results count for the team total. The team gains points by winning or drawing rated games. Points are weighted, with results in higher sections worth more. ------------------------------------------------- Mohar February Chess Tournament – Scholastic and Open Chess Tournament February 21, 2026 Holiday Inn, 909 Holcomb Bridge Rd Roswell, GA 30076 4SS, G/25;d5 5 sections – An Open section for adults and advanced scholastic players, 3 Rated Scholastic-only sections for K-12 players and a Nonrated Scholastic practice section for new and young players. ROUND TIMES: First round is at 10:00AM, rounds 2-4 will start ASAP after the preceding rounds finish with a slightly longer break for lunch between rounds 2 and 3. We are usually done around 4 – 4:30 PM. NONRATED SECTION: The Nonrated section is for new/unrated players and players rated below 300 who need practice. While the rules of chess still apply, this is a more relaxed game designed to let new and young players experience chess without worrying about ratings. New players may choose to play in the Under 400 section if they want to become rated. 3 SCHOLASTIC-ONLY RATED SECTIONS: Under 400, Under 800 and Under 1200: These sections require an active US Chess Federation membership (https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess). New players wanting a rating play in the Under 400. OPEN SECTION: This Section is available to both adults and scholastic players. Scholastic players rated over 1199 must play in this section; however, any scholastic player rated 1000+ may choose to play in either the Open or kids-only Under 1200 section. Players will be placed in the section that matches their rating unless granted an exemption by the Tournament Director. Rated sections may be combined at TD discretion. ENTRY FEE: Early entry received through 10th February is $35. Registration is $40 from February 11 - 19. Late registration begins February 20th and is $45. Same day, onsite registration is $50 and must be completed by 9:00AM to be paired for Round 1. Late sign ups may receive a ½ point round one bye. REGISTRATION: CLICK HERE , fill out the form, and pay via Zelle to [email protected] BYES: If you have a scheduling conflict and plan to skip one or two rounds, 1/2 Point Byes are available and should be requested at the time of registration. INDIVIDUAL PRIZES: Trophies for 1st, 2nd, 3rd place in each SCHOLASTIC section and cash or gift cards for the Open section. TEAM PRIZES: Team Trophies to top 3 schools based on weighted points of 4 players. Must have a minimum of 3 players from the same school playing in the USCF Rated Sections to qualify for Team Prizes. FOOD – We plan to have food vendors to supply snacks and lunch. Sets, boards and notation sheets supplied. Please bring chess clocks if possible. At-Risk-Youth Seniors Women menu arrow_back TEXAS ACTION CHAMPIONSHIP 2026 Grand Prix, State Championship Event THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO Saturday, February 21, 2026 Event Overview Texas Action Championship 2026 A US Chess Grand Prix and State Championship Event At The Houston Chess Studio Saturday, Feb. 21 2026 REGISTRATION: https://www.kingregistration.com/event/ACTION_CHAMP_2026 Event Overview: A one-day event. 5 Round Swiss, G/30, d5. 3 Sections: Open, U1600, U800 Projected Prizes: $900.00 Including $300 Guaranteed 1st Place , Grand Prix Points and 2026 Texas Action Chess Champion title and trophy for First Place in the Open Section Benefits: 1. State Championship Status Do you want to be known as the best chess player in Texas for one-hour games? As an official US Chess state championship, sponsored by the Texas Chess Association, we have the honor of making this possible by awarding the title of “2026 Texas Action Chess Champion.” 2. Grand Prix Event This tournament is one of the very few upcoming events in Texas that qualify as a US Chess Grand Prix event. In case you are not familiar with the US Chess Grand Prix, it is a US Chess program that recognizes the ten players who win the most points in qualifying Grand Prix events. Essentially, if you make it into the top ten, it is proof that you are among the best of the best. It also means that you receive a substantial cash prize from US Chess. 3. Beginners Are Welcome This tournament is not just for high-rated players. There will be two under sections (U1600 & U800) so that players can compete against other players of similar ability and are not crushed by opponents they have no chance of defeating anytime soon. But if you want to ‘play up’ into the Open Section you can do so for no additional charge. The Texas Action Championship will also be one of the very few cash prize events that offers a U800 section. 4. Savings Potential We recognize the hardships of inflation. Accordingly, our starting entry fees ($45 for the Open and $35 for all other sections) are much lower than the entry fees that are charged as we move closer to the event. If you want a deal, register now. Not sure if you can come yet? No need to worry. Your entry fee is fully refundable until seven days before the event. No questions asked. No hassle. Just ask for a refund by the deadline and your refund will be on its way in no time. If you cancel within 7 days of the event you will be refunded the entry fee minus $15 OR you may apply the entire entry fee to a future event, within 90 days, at The Houston Chess Studio. The Fine Print: Qualifications : All chess players, regardless of residence, are welcome as long as they meet the membership requirements. You must have an unexpired USCF and TCA membership in good standing on the day of the tournament. If you do not have these memberships at the moment, you can still register but you will need to purchase/renew them before the tournament. Please note, however, that while residents of other states may participate and win cash prizes, the state champion title and trophy are for Texas residents only. Entry Fees : For the Open Section, $45 by Jan 3rd; $55 by Feb. 7th; $65 thereafter. For all other sections, $35 by Jan. 3rd; $45 by Feb. 7th; $55 thereafter. Byes: Every player is entitled to one half point bye if requested before the close of online registration. All last round byes are for zero points. Draws: Draws prior to 30 moves and both players are barred from any cash prizes and the state champion title. Schedule : Round 1, 10:00-11:00am; Round 2, 11:15am-12:15pm; Lunch Break; Round 3, 1:00-2:00pm; Round 4, 2:15-3:15pm; and; Round 5, 3:30-4:30pm. Prizes : For the Open section, $300 for first place plus a trophy, $150 for second place. $300 First Place in the Open Section is guaranteed , all other cash prizes based on 50 total paid entries . For all other sections, $150 for first place, $75 for second place. In the event of ties, prizes will be equally divided between the tying players in conformity with the Official Rules of Chess. However, if two or more Texas residents tie for first place in the Open Section, all of them will be recognized as co-champions, but tie breaks will determine who takes home the trophy. All cash prizes paid via PayPal. Notation: Absent a physical or developmental disability rendering a player unable to notate, notation is required in all sections except the U800 section. Equipment : Bring your own chess boards and pieces and clock if you have them. Some will be provided by the organizer but maybe not enough for everyone. You can still play even if you do not own a chess clock. Electronic notation approved by US Chess will be allowed and notation sheets will be provided free of charge as well. Section Assignment : You may ‘play up’ if you want, at no additional charge. If you initially register for an under section and then move to the Open section, you will be charged a $10 section adjustment fee because the entry fee for the Open is higher to allow for larger prizes. However, this fee will not apply if you were allowed to play in an under section when you registered but later are required to play in the Open section because your rating increased after registration. The tournament Director reserves the right to merge sections if necessary. Rating : This tournament will use your regular rating as shown on the February Supplement for the purposes of section qualification and pairings. Players with foreign ratings are required to disclose such ratings and the tournament director may make such adjustments to the deemed rating of said players as he thinks proper. Unrated Policy : Unrated players may win a maximum of $100, unless they are playing in the Open Section, in which case there are no limitations to how much they can win. If no rating is assigned, an unrated player may choose any section. Illegal Moves: As a variation of the Official Rules of Chess, an illegal move that is not corrected within three moves shall stand. The default rule is that illegal moves may be corrected up to ten moves away. The organizer believes that a lookback of up to ten moves is impracticable for events with shorter time controls like the Texas Action Championship. Spectators: No spectators will be allowed in the Tournament Hall while games are underway. However, there is a skittles room/lounge right next door inside the Houston Chess Studio. Many of the ongoing games, and views of the entire tournament hall, will be visible on one of the many screens on display in the lounge. Food : There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza. Several others are within walking distance. There are also vending machines located in the skittles room/lounge of The Studio. Food and beverages are allowed at the playing boards. Just be sure to clean up after yourself. Venue: THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO provides a quality chess playing experience for players of all levels, and their parents and spectators . Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009. Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45. There is always plenty of FREE parking at The Studio. At-Risk-Youth Seniors Women menu arrow_back 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships NYOS Charter School Saturday, February 21, 2026 Event Overview Would you like to be an Austin area scholastic chess champion? Here’s your chance! Scholastic chess tournament in multiple sections to be held on February 21, 2026. G/25, +5 inc. Trophies and medals awarded. Full pairings and standings can be found at the registration link below (click on the blue “Live” text to get to them). Register HERE ! When you click the link, scroll to the bottom for registration. See Preregistration List HERE Basics USCF rated chess tournament in multiple RATED scholastic sections: K-3 U400, K-3 U700, K-5 U600, K-5 U1000, 6-12 U600, 6-12 U1000, and K-12 Elite (for players rated 950-1399). Please note: all scholastic players rated 1400 and over must play in the Open section . Please note, at the event pairings will be posted only online . This is a Swiss-system tournament, so everyone plays all day—there is no “elimination.” Players must know how to play the game of chess! We follow US Chess rules including: touch-move, mandatory clocks if available, and notation. K-3 and younger sections are excused from taking notation. Please review the Parent/Coach Responsibilities before registering. Location NYOS Charter School 12333 N Lamar Blvd Austin, TX 78753 Eligibility This is a rated tournament. You must have a USCF ID and your membership can be purchased/renewed online with US Chess in advance of registration. You can verify your US Chess membership ID and expiration by visiting the US Chess Member Services Area . Anyone can become a USCF member. Players new to tournament chess are welcome to play. Your US Chess membership cannot expire before February 28, 2026. (New players in 3rd grade and below may request a non-member ID as a part of USCF’s Junior Tournament Player program during registration. JTPs ok in K-3 sections only .) “Under” sections are only for students meeting the rating criteria. All players who are new to tournaments are eligible for their age appropriate ‘under’ section. ( Look up your player’s rating here . Please email the registrar or ask your chess coach for placement information. If your 6th grader attends an Elementary School, please contact the registrar for options. With enough registrations, any section may be divided into two sections so we can offer more prizes. Sections with fewer than 20 entries may be merged into a similar section to provide optimal pairings and competition. Please note: February 2026 ‘Regular’ OTB ratings will be used for pairing purposes. If no regular rating is available, then other USCF ratings (quick, blitz, online) can and will be considered for section placement. Requests to play down will not be honored. FYI: Any event that is rated after January 21st will not affect your February supplement rating, as those events takes place after February ratings are calculated. All players in this event must be in 12th grade or lower. Schedule No check-in necessary for preregistrations. We will make every attempt to contact you in advance if we see a problem with your registration. Verify your entry online! 8:00 a.m. Chess Control opens for onsite registration. Onsite registrations before 9:30am accepted, but must start play in round 2. 8:30 a.m Announcements begin in all scholastic playing rooms. Players and coaches should be present. 9:00 a.m. Rd 1 begins. Scholastic sections have 5 rds, G/25, +5. 9:00 a.m. Open section (different event allowing adults) begins. Open has 4 rounds, all rounds are are G/45, +5. 9:15 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Chess control open for event issues. No changes for round 1 (bye or section) allowed after online registration closes. Requests for byes, withdrawals, and player or school information edits go in effect immediately if made via email before the close of online registration. Changes requested onsite go into effect as of round 2. Approximate Round Times Scholastic Sections: round 1 – 9:00am, rd 2 – 11:00am, rd 3 – 12:45 pm, rd 4 – 2:30 pm, rd 5 – 4:00 pm Awards in the cafeteria as each section finishes. Notes There will be some down time between rounds since many games will finish early. We will provide an area (outside the tournament room) for casual “skittles” chess and/or other indoor activities. Parents and/or coaches, please provide age-appropriate activities during the time between rounds. The organizers cannot baby-sit. No child should be left unattended! Concessions details coming soon. Only water bottles allowed at the chess board. Awards Trophies & Medals to Top Contenders! Ribbons to all participants! Trophies to the top individuals in each scholastic section. Trophies to the top teams in all sections. Number of individual and team trophies will depend on number of entries. Chess medals will go to all players (excluding Open section) that finish the tournament with a positive score (3.0 & 3.5 points). Trophies to players scoring 4.0 and above. No teams in Open section, but special trophies will be awarded to the highest scoring Family & Child teams (Uncles, Aunts, Adult siblings, Parents, Grandparents, or coach paired with at least one scholastic aged player.) Registration Information *$35 thru Saturday, 1/31/2026. *$45 thru Saturday, 2/14/2026. *Late entry $50 begins Sunday, 2/15/2026 and ENDS at midnight on Wednesday, 2/18/2026, at which time online entry closes. *$60 Onsite entry receives 1/2pt bye in round 1, and begins play in round 2. Withdrawals requested via email before online registration closes ( midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26) are eligible for a refund (minus a $10 service fee). No exceptions. No refunds for USCF memberships after purchased from the USCF. NO email/phone entries. Please request byes by adding a note when you register. First bye receives 1/2-point. Further byes receive 0-points. Email the registrar to make changes to your requested byes. Deadline to add or remove a 1st round requested bye is 9am Friday 2/20/2026. All 1/2-point byes must be requested/removed before the end of round 2. Email Click here to show mail address with other questions. No phone calls, please. Emails will be returned promptly. On site registration first come, first serve. Tournament details: Five round, two-section, swiss system, G/40;d5, USCF dual-rated tournament. Date: Saturday, February 21, 2026. Registration 9:15 AM-9:45 AM, first round pairs for 10:00 AM. Please do not enter the building prior to 9:15 AM! Venue: Baton Rouge Bridge Center, 3033 Old Forge Dr, Baton Rouge, LA Round times: 10:00 AM, 11:45 AM, 1:25PM, [meal break], 3:45 PM, 5:25 PM, prizes at 7:00 PM. Round times are tentative and subject to change. If we can move quicker, we will! Prize fund: Prize fund is $1,000 b/60, 50% guaranteed. Prize fund breakdown as follows: 1st in open/unrated, $400 2nd in open/unrated, $200 1st in u1400, $250 2nd in u1400, $150 Sections: Open and U1400. Open section is FIDE rated and directed according to FIDE rules. Players should familiarize themselves with the most common FIDE rules differences . TD reserves the right to adjust sections to match turnout. TDs reserve the right to use accelerated swiss pairing if one section contains more than 32 players. Pairing: Highest of quick or regular rating to be used for pairing and prizes. If you are rated under 1400 but would like to play in the open, you may register for the open at no extra charge. Unrated players may play in either section, but are prize eligible in the open only. Ratings determined by this month's official USCF rating. 100 elo may be added to those with provisional ratings. Entry fee: $35 early entry fee if purchased by one week prior. $40 standard entry if purchased by two days prior. $45 thereafter and on-site. Capacity limited to first 80 registrants. Eligibility: Current USCF membership required. FIDE membership required for open section. FIDE membership is free if you already have a USCF membership (we will register you). No FIDE rated players 2400 or above, due to time control and format. Bye policy: Two 0.5 point byes for any round available upon request, must be made prior to pairing round three in non-emergency situations. Bye requests cannot be cancelled following the start of round 3. Equipment: A small amount of chess equipment will be provided. If you have a chess set and clock, please bring it. Tiebreaks: Cash prizes to be split among all tied entrants. Late arrivals: Games are forfeited 30 minutes after the round start time if a player has not arrived. Refunds: Players who withdraw 60 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%). FIDE rated: Top section played in accordance with the FIDE Laws of Chess. 2026 Event Overview USCF rated chess tournament on February 21, 2026 for adults and more advanced scholastic players. 4 round Swiss at G/45 +5. Full pairings and standings can be found at the registration link below (click on the blue “Live” text to get to them). Register HERE ! When you click the link, scroll to the bottom for registration. See Preregistration List HERE Basics This is a Swiss-system tournament, so everyone plays all day—there is no “elimination.” Players must know how to play the game of chess! We follow USCF rules including: touch-move, mandatory clocks (bring your own if at all possible), and mandatory notation. If registrations exceed 32, we reserve the right to split into two sections. Location NYOS Charter School 12333 N Lamar Blvd Austin, TX 78753 Eligibility All adults Any youth who have reached at least 1300 by the February 2026 USCF supplement. Ineligible entries will be moved to the appropriate scholastic section of the 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships . This is a rated tournament. You must have a USCF ID and your membership (can be purchased/renewed at check out or online with the USCF in advance of registration) . You can verify your USCF membership ID and expiration by visiting the USCF’s Member Services Area . Anyone can become a USCF member. Players new to tournament chess are welcome to play. Your USCF membership cannot expire before February 28, 2026. Schedule No check-in necessary for preregistrations. We will make every attempt to contact you in advance if we see a problem with your registration. Verify your entry ONLINE! 9:00 a.m. Open section begins. Open has 4 rounds, all rounds are are G/45, +5. No changes for round 1 (bye or section) allowed after online registration closes. Requests for byes, withdrawals, player info edits be made onsite with your chief TD and go into effect as of round 2. Approximate Round Times Open Section: rd 1 – 9:00am, rd2 – 11:00am, rd3 – 1:30pm, rd4 – 3:30pm Notes There will be some down time between rounds since many games will finish early. We will provide an area (outside the tournament room) for casual “skittles” chess and/or other indoor activities. Concessions TBA. Only water bottles allowed at the chess board. Awards Cash prizes (to winners in both sections, in the case of multiple sections), based on number of entries. Special trophies will be awarded to the highest scoring Family & Child teams (Uncles, Aunts, Adult siblings, Parents, or Grandparents paired with at least one scholastic aged player.). Registration Information Entry fee pricing is staggered and based on date of entry/payment. *youth – $35/adult – $25 through Saturday, 1/31/2026. *youth – $45/adult – $35 through Saturday, 2/14/2026. *Late entry youth-$50 / adult – $40 begins Sunday, 2/15/2026 and ENDS at midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26, at which time online entry closes. *If space permits, onsite registration on Saturday, 2/21/26 will be permitted, $50 regardless of age. Cash or venmo only. First round play requires registration and payment before 8:45am. Withdrawals requested via email before midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26 are eligible for a refund (minus a $10 service fee). No exceptions. NO email/phone entries. If you need byes, request them by adding a note when you register. First bye receives 1/2-point. Further byes receive 0-points. Email the registrar to make changes to your requested byes. Deadline to add or remove a 1st round requested bye is 9am Friday 2/20/2026. All 1/2-point byes must be requested/removed before the end of round 2. Email Sarah Brauner ( Click here to show mail address ) with other questions. No phone calls, please. Emails will be returned promptly.
