Sunday, March 22, 2026 Event Overview 5th Annual Old Line Open Rockville, Maryland Individual Registration Group Registration Championship, U2100, U1900, U1700, U1500: 5SS, Game/90 inc/30 -- (2-day schedule: Rnds 1-2 Game/45 inc/30) U1250 and U1000 : 5SS, Game/75 d/5 with Rnds 1-2 at Game/45 d/5; U1250 3-day schedule : all rounds Game/75 d/5 Playing Site Rockville Hilton, Rockville, MD We aim to create a pleasant environment for playing chess. Below are the answers we received at a previous tournament to the question of what do we do better than other tournaments. Advance Entries Tournament Features We pair rounds as early as possible and start rounds on time → You have time to get ready and don't have to waste your time waiting for the round to start 30" increment time control in the top five sections → No more clock smashing scrambles at the end of the game. Score-based prizes → See the advantages below. Additional 1st place prizes to clear first when there is no 5-0 player in the section, added to your score prize → More prize money Minimum ratings to play in the top 5 sections → Less mismatch games. Sets, boards and clocks provided for everyone → No more carrying around pieces and a board, just bring a clock. Free Sunday morning Continental breakfast → Relax, have some coffee and a danish before you start your game. Texting or emailing of pairings to your cell phone available → No rush at the pairing chart before the round $149 hotel rate, Reserve a room → Relax and stay at the tournament hotel. $5 EF discount if staying at hotel. Hotel next to DC Metro stop → Take the Metro directly to the tournament. Shorter time controls in lower sections → Less waiting around between rounds. Prizes This tournament will pay prizes based solely on your final score. All the prizes are guaranteed. If the total pay out in the Open section is less than $1500, extra money will be added to the pay out of the top score group to bring the total to $1500. Advantages over place-based scoring Less Waiting Your score determines your prize. Once you finish your last game, you can receive a check. Less Uncertainty Your prize does not get lowered if others tie with you. For example, if there are two 5-0 players, both receive the full amount for 5-0. Less short draws The total payout is always higher when games are decisive. All unrateds and are limited to a maximum prize of $100 in the U1000, $200 in the U1300, and $400 in the U1500 section. Balance goes to player(s) with same score or is divided among players in next lower score group. Entrance Fees Early (online or mail by 2/21) $129 Regular (online or mail by 3/4) $139 Late (online by 3/6) $149 At-the-door (cash or credit card ) $160. Advance Entries Special Entrance Fees Under 1250 section: all entrance fees $45 less. Under 1000: all entrance fees $65 less. Free early entrance to GMs. nothing will be subtracted from any prizes. $45 discount EF for IMs . nothing will be subtracted from any prizes. $5 discount if staying at hotel. Individual Registration Group Registration Mail Registrations to: Maryland Chess Assn. 1827 Thornton Ridge Road Towson, MD 21204 Mailed registrations should include name, section, schedule(2-day or 3-day). The chief TD for the tournament will be Mike Regan. If you have any questions about the tournament email him at [email protected] . Advance Registrations Schedules 3-day schedule Champ - U1500: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds. Fri 7 pm, Saturday 11am and 5:30, Sunday 9:30 am and 2:45. 2-day schedule Champ - U1500: Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Saturday 11am, 2:15 and 5:30, Sunday 9:30 am and 2:45. U1000 and U1250 2-day schedule: Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Saturday 11, 12:45 and 3:00, Sunday 9:30 am and 12:15 pm. U1250 3-day schedule: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds Friday 7 pm, Saturday 11 and 3:00, Sunday 9:30 am and 12:15 pm. Byes Half point byes: all must commit before rd 3 Reentries: all, $80 except U1000 and U1250 $40. You can reenter any schedule taking 1/2 point byes for unplayed games. If you reenter with a single 1/2 point bye, the cost is $70/$35. If you reenter with two 1/2 point byes, the cost is $60/$30. Hotel Rates: $149 per night $5 EF discount if staying at hotel. Reserve a room Parking : $6 for day guest and $10 overnight. Parking is free in Metro parking lot over the weekend. Rooms are limited. So make your reservations early. Rule Variations In sections that the organizer provides clocks, if both players are not present at the start of the round, the tournament director will start white's clock. Clocks that halt on end are preferred in all sections with increment time controls. Any player forfeiting a round must pay a $50 fine before being allowed to play in a future tournament organized by MCA or Baltimore Chess. The electronic score keeping devices, ChessNoteR and eNotate, cannot be used at this tournament. All players with provisional ratings will have 100 points added to their rating for determining section eligibility Players with byes who are eligible to play in a lower section that also has a bye player may get paired in that section as a house player. They will still have the bye for standings in their original section. The game in the lower section does count for standings and must be played. The TD will specify which direction the clocks must face. The provided clocks will be set to "halt on end". FIDE rated sections will use FIDE rules. A summary of the differences is here. Phone Rules All phones should be off. Phones should not be on your person when you leave the room. In non-FIDE rated sections you can store you phone on the table or in a bag next to your chair. Phone lockers are available for all sections. Any with ringing phone or leaving (or returning to ) the playing hall with a phone will receive a time reduction of 30 minutes or half your remaining time which ever is less. Anyone using their phone to affect the game will be forfeited. USCF Dual Rated Open to players who are EITHER age 14 and older OR whose US Chess Current Published Regular Rating for the month of the tournament is 900 or higher. US Chess Membership is required. Three Sections Section Gold: 1700 and over (1600 - 1699 may play up to Gold) Section Silver: 1200-1699 (1100 - 1199 may play up to Silver) Section Bronze: U1200 and unrated Sections may be combined at TD discretion. IMPORTANT: We use the US Chess Current Published Regular rating for the month of the tournament to place players in sections. We don’t make exceptions. Junior players: Junior players (under fourteen years) rated 900+ are welcome. Must be accompanied by an adult throughout the event. We do not accept junior players rated under 900. Three rounds. Digital clocks are required and will be set to G/60, delay 5 . You may take one half-point bye in round 1 or round 2. Prizes: Your prize is an excellent playing experience at a reasonable cost. We've been running these since 2007 and people like playing here. Entry fee is $20. Please pre-register and pay here when registration opens. Online registration closes when the tournament is full; we don’t have a wait list; we reopen registration if spaces become available. On-Site Entries: Check evanstonchess.org the morning of the tournament. If space is available on-site entries for $20 cash are taken on an as-available basis starting at 9:00 a.m. Master and Expert Entries: First two Masters or Experts who sign up get free entry. If your USCF or FIDE regular rating is 2000 or higher, email your name and USCF ID to Click here to show mail address by 5 p.m. the Tuesday before the tournament to pre-register. Schedule: Check-in and On-site Registration from 9:00 to 9:30 AM. Players must check in on the posted registration list by 9:30 am; players who don’t check in receive a half-point bye for the first round or will be paired with another late arrival. First Round 9:50 am, last round over roughly 5:00 pm. Bring your lunch! We will have a brief lunch break with no time to go out for food. On-site we have vending machine snacks, coffee and soft drinks. Other information: Sets supplied. Bring digital delay clocks. Wheelchair accessible. No Smoking. Limit 50 players. Battle on the BB-64 A chess tournament on the ship! Norfolk, Virginia March 21, 2026 REGISTER HERE: Battle on the BB-64 Hampton Roads Chess Association and Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin join forces to present the third annual chess tournament to be held on board the Battleship Wisconsin (BB-64) docked at Nauticus on the Norfolk Waterfront! Games will be played in the Crew Mess, where sailors from WWII to Operation Desert Storm dined while underway! There is a LOT of information to share for this event, and most questions can be answered below. Please read thoroughly! By registering and attending in this event (as participant or guest), you acknowledge and agree to abide by the US Chess Federation's Safe Play Policy , and HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release. More details below. Registration for this event closes at 11:59pm EST on Thursday, March 19th! No last-minute or on-site registration! This is an HRCA Scholastic Cup Event! HRCA membership is not required for the tournament but IS required to participate in the Scholastic Cup awards. New Memberships must be purchased within one week of event conclusion for points to qualify. For more information visit https://hrchessclub.org/scholastic-cup/ SCHEDULE 9:15-10:00 AM - Recommended time to arrive for parking and walking to the venue. Check-in table to pick up pre-ordered wristbands on the deck outside the main entry to the Nauticus will be open by 9:30AM. 10:00 AM - Doors open 11:00 AM -- Round 1 12:15 PM -- Round 2 1:30 PM -- Round 3 2:45 PM -- Round 4 3:45 PM -- Awards in the Brock Theater 4:45 PM -- Photos on the fantail 5:00 PM -- Everyone must be off the ship / Nauticus closes PARTICIPANTS ***NEW THIS YEAR -- THIS IS AN ALL-AGES EVENT!!!*** Players under age 14 require an adult to be onsite for the duration of the event -- All guests must have a Nauticus day pass (see below). We have a special group rate through March 19th. After that, you may purchase regular admission or utilize any discount programs directly with the front desk. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS: US Chess membership is required for Open, Amateur, and Novice -- these are rated sections. US Chess membership is NOT required for Rookie sections. HRCA membership is only required if you want your points counted for the HRCA Scholastic Cup. FORMAT A Swiss System (like a bracket system -- NOT an elimination event! ) tournament of four rounds. Time control is G/25; d3, meaning each side has 25 minutes to complete all their moves, and the clock will not start counting down for the first 3 seconds of each move. Select a bye during registration ONLY if you know you will be missing a round due to a conflict with another event. One half-point bye allowed if requested prior to the start of Round 3. Boards, sets, and clocks are provided. Notation is NOT required in any section due to Quick time control, but notation sheets and pencils will be provided if desired. Section choices are: K-3 Rookie: Grades Pre-K through 3rd with little to no tournament experience. No rated players allowed. US Chess membership is not required. K-6 Rookie: For youth in grades 4th-6th with little to no tournament experience. No rated players allowed. US Chess membership is not required. Senior Rookie : For ADULTS and youth in grades 7th-12th with little to no tournament experience. No rated players allowed. US Chess membership is not required. Scholastic Novice (U300): Youth in grades PK-12th who are US Chess members with a Regular over-the-board (OTB) rating Under 300. The March supplement will be used. Unrated players are allowed in the Novice section and are eligible for place prizes or Top Unrated prizes only. Amateur (U800): All ages who are US Chess members with Regular over-the-board (OTB) rating Under 800. The March supplement will be used. Unrated players are allowed in the Amateur section and are eligible for place prizes only. Open: All ages who are US Chess members -- unrated or of any rating -- but designed for players rated over 800. Playing up is allowed. Unrated players are allowed in the Open section and are eligible for place prizes only. The March supplement will be used. A note on Unrated players: Per new US Chess Scholastic Regulations, HRCA will apply the current Regular OTB rating to Unrated players, if applicable, even if earned after the cut-off for the supplement used for the tournament. In a dual-rated event, if there is no Regular OTB rating, a current Quick rating will be applied, if applicable, but only for prizes, not sectioning (e.g. someone with a 500 published Quick rating but Unrated Regular may still play in the U300 section but is ineligible for Unrated prizes). Bottom line -- only actually Unrated players at the time of the event will be allowed in Rookie sections and eligible for Unrated class prizes in rated sections. Check your US Chess membership here AWARDS Individual: TROPHIES to the Top 5 finishers in each section. Trophy to Top U1000 in Open. Trophies to Top U500 in Amateur and Top Unrated in Novice. Trophy to Top K-1 in K-3 Rookie. Medals to additional players with at least 2 points. Participation ribbons to all remaining players. Team: A team is comprised of two or more players from the same school, with the top four scores counting toward the team score. Team awards will be cross-section with trophies for Top 3 Elementary Schools and Top 2 Middle Schools. Top High School trophy will be added only if more than one high school team enters by March 9th. ENTRY FEE $35 Early Entry Fee through 11:59 PM on Sunday, February 22nd. $40 Standard Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Sunday, March 8th. $45 Late Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Sunday, March 15th. $50 Last Week Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Thursday, March 19th. TOURNAMENT REGISTRATION WILL CLOSE AT 11:59 PM ON MARCH 19th. NO EXCEPTIONS. NO WALKUPS. There are no scholarship or Title 1 entry fee waivers for this event. REFUNDS If you need to withdraw, please contact the Event Organizer. Refunds will be given as a tournament credit ONLY. Refunds create a lot of administrative work and loss of important operational revenue to HRCA. Our default refund is to now give participants a CREDIT towards a future HRCA tournament. The credited amount will be $30 and is valid for 1 year. After February 8th, there is a 50% credit. No refunds after February 19th. ** Please check the ENTRY LIST before registering to make sure you do not register multiple times. Duplicate entries are subject to an administrative refund fee of $10. Nauticus guest tickets must be purchased separately and are NOT refundable. Tournament Orientation for New Players There will be no New Player Orientation the day of the event -- Use this link and passcode for a recording of a complete orientation to tournament procedures and rules. https://us02web.zoom.us/rec/share/k1QA3hzoj0hYP7z5uwD7DYE2Mn-atQYhQO6YHRxyvfL_FDVO5HqW1C_6MDyyTNmv.NxHuuWAIwUzGT4sB Passcode: h.8mre41 A copy of the slides will be sent to all registered players the evening of March 19th. For an earlier copy, contact the event organizer. Special Notes for Event Day PARKING : Adjacent garages are approximately $13 a day; the MacArthur Center garage within walking distance is $1 a day on weekends! MEALS : No outside food or drink is allowed inside Nauticus or the Battleship. For anyone bringing their own lunch and eating on the front porch, they have a lunch bin system. Guests can drop their lunches in the bin at check-in, and they’ll wheel it into storage. At lunchtime, you can bring it back out to the porch. If you leave the museum, your wristband will give you re-entry. Please make sure your player knows where to find you or designate another adult to supervise if you leave the premises without your player. Be aware the tournament rounds are very close together, so do not depart the site with your player and risk missing a round. The on-site cafe is under new management, and they are offering pre-orders of box lunches, which is strongly recommended to get your food on time for your player to eat between rounds -- Click here for a menu . CLICK HERE TO PRE-ORDER LUNCH . WAITING AREAS ("SKITTLES") : Please enjoy the venue and pack light (you may go back to your vehicle if needed). All players and accompanying family members / friends are strongly encouraged to explore Nauticus and the Battleship between rounds! Camp chairs are not permitted at the venue. The Brock Theater on the 3rd floor of Nauticus is the main waiting area for parents. This will be open to all museum guests, so please be mindful of others enjoying the space and secure your belongings. A short film will be shown at 11am and 2pm for all museum guests. YOU MAY NOT USE THE NAUTICUS CAFE AS A WAITING AREA. Volunteers will be enforcing this. *Parents of younger children who may not be able to navigate from the ship's crew mess back to Nauticus will be allowed to wait in the galley (standing) next to the crew mess. Please make sure your players know where to find you after each round! BATHROOMS : There is ample access to public bathrooms in Nauticus. There is one bathroom available on the deck of the ship prior to descending the stairs to the crew mess. We STRONGLY urge parents to ensure their kids use the bathroom BEFORE the start of a round. Once the round has started, getting a child back and forth to a bathroom on the ship is challenging. HANDICAPPED ACCESSIBILITY : Access to the ship's galley requires the physical ability to climb up and down one short but steep ladder. Players unable to make that climb can contact us in advance to make arrangements for an alternative assigned board in an accessible area of the ship or Nauticus. Discounted Group Nauticus/Battleship Tickets : Required for all guests. Admission to Nauticus and the Battleship is included in the entry fee for players only. IMPORTANT - After registering your player for the tournament, go to 2026 Battle on the BB-64 ADMISSION tickets to purchase your group rate admission tickets for family members or friends accompanying the player. You will receive a wristband upon arrival for entry. These tickets are non-refundable. Your PLAYER'S admission is included in their entry fee - do NOT purchase a ticket for registered players. For accompanying parents / siblings / guests, the group admission rates (tax included) are: $15 for students (ages 3-17) $18 for adults (ages 18+) ages 0-2 free but must be listed on reservation NO PLAYER UNDER THE AGE OF 14 MAY BE DROPPED OFF / UNACCOMPANIED FOR THIS EVENT. Carpooling is welcome. All players under age 14 must have a designated adult onsite for the duration of the day. Group sales end March 19th at 11:59PM -- No exceptions. Regular admission fees may be paid at the door the day of event. Please visit the Nauticus website for any other eligible discounts and ticket reservations if not purchasing group tickets through HRCA. You will receive a confirmation with check-in instructions when you order tickets through HRCA. VOLUNTEERS NEEDED ! Volunteers help ensure our events run smoothly and that players and families have an enjoyable experience. Volunteer spots include set up, clean up, wristband distribution, player escorts (Safe Play certification required), scorekeepers, CERTIFIED Tournament Directors (TDs), and assistant/junior TDs (not certified). Key (all-day) volunteers receive complimentary entry. Sign up to volunteer for a part of the day here: Hampton Roads Chess Association: Battle on BB-64 CONTACT US Please contact the Tournament Organizer: For more information/questions, contact the Tournament Organizer, Tina, at [email protected] or 757-472-5909. Email is the fastest way to reach us. POLICIES AND RULES It is our goal to provide a fun, safe, and supportive environment. Community partnerships are vital to HRCA, and we want to ensure we remain good stewards to our partners and their facilities. There is a lot of downtime during tournaments -- parents are responsible for supervising their children when they are not playing a scheduled match. Please note only designated areas of the facility are open to players and guests. No one is allowed in undesignated areas (including classrooms) at any time. No drop-offs for youth under age 14. By registering and attending in this event (as participant or guest), you acknowledge and agree to abide by the US Chess Federation's Safe Play Policy , and HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release. For more information on Safe Play or HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release, please click the BLUE links above. Violations of these policies may result in warnings, or ultimately, disqualification or dismissal from the event without refund. Photo Policy: Please be advised that photos and/or videos may be taken at HRCA events for use in HRCA's marketing, grant reporting, educational, news, or other promotional materials, whether in print, electronic, or other forms of media, including on our website and social channels. HRCA will not identify images using the full names of those photographed without express written permission. By attending an HRCA event, you consent to have your image recorded for distribution and agree to release, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify HRCA from any and all claims, including compensation, involving using your picture or likeness. If you wish to opt-out, you can make your wishes known to the photographer, and/or the event organizers, and/or contact HRCA at Click here to show mail address . Seniors Women menu arrow_back K-12 Under 1200 Swiss The Pingry School Saturday, March 21, 2026 Event Overview K-12 Under 1200 Swiss Tournament Our tournaments are open to K-12 students rated under 1200 from any school! This tournament has three sections based on age and rating, and players will only play opponents in their section. All sections begin at 9am, and they are all four rounds and non-elimination. No one will be allowed to play if they are not on the Entry List. (If you are a new player or not sure if this is the right event/section, please email Click here to show mail address or join our WhatsApp Group to inquire which event link should be used.) NOTES: SCCF Membership is mandatory for all SoCal Residents playing in Championship sections! Register/Renew SCCF Membership here . (If you're unsure whether your SCCF membership will expire or needs renewal before SuperStates begins, please check here .) Each Championship section has a minimum rating requirement. If you are a beginner or do not yet have a rating, we recommend registering for the Junior Varsity sections here instead. The tournament is USCF-rated, but not FIDE-rated. The March 2026 Supplement Rating will be used for pairing. Chess sets will be provided. Please bring your chess clock. Sections Champ K-12 (Minimum rating of 1000) Champ Girls (Minimum rating of 800) Champ K-8 (Minimum rating of 800) Champ K-5 (Minimum rating of 600) Champ K-3 (Minimum rating of 400) NOTE: Please be aware of the minimum rating requirements for each Championship section. Section eligibility will be determined based on a player’s peak rating (including provisioning rating) between November 1 and March 15 . The only exception is when a team must include a player below the minimum rating to complete a 4-player team. In such cases, please email [email protected] to request an exception. Girls may participate in any section for which they meet the rating requirements. Only girls may participate in the Championship Girls Section . Please review the information below regarding eligibility for SoCal Representatives for the corresponding National Invitationals . State Qualifier Eligibility To be eligible to qualify as a Southern California State Representative from a Championship section, players must meet all of the following requirements: SoCal residency (billing address or supporting documentation may be requested for verification). Valid SCCF membership at the time of the tournament. Enrolled in a U.S. school , including public, private, or state-approved homeschooling programs (the curriculum must be approved by the state). Cannot represent another state for National Invitational competitions in the same year. Note: Players who do not meet all eligibility requirements may still compete in Championship sections but will not be eligible for State titles or National Invitational qualification. Format: 6SS, G/80, d/10 Rounds: Day 1 – Saturday Day 2 – Sunday 9:00 am — Opening Ceremony 9:00 am — Round 4 10:00 am — Round 1 1:00 pm — Round 5 2:00 pm — Round 2 4:00 pm — Round 6 5:00 pm — Round 3 7:30 pm — Champion Awards Ceremony 2 half-point byes are allowed, but not in final round. Half-point byes need to be submitted before March 21st, 2026 Entry Fee: Early Bird: $110 (by Jan. 31st) Regular: $130 (by Feb. 28th) Late Entry: $160 (by March 13th) Free Entry for IMs/GMs (by Feb. 28th) Event Cancellation Policy $10 Cancellation Fee until Jan. 31st. Then, until 3/15, $20. No refunds at all if you cancel after March 15th. Submit a Change Request here (change.SuperStates.org) for a withdrawal. Sunday, March 22, 2026 Event Overview 2026 Sioux Falls Open City Chess Championship Dates: March 21-22 Event Site: 3000 S. Minnesota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD (2nd Floor Conference Area of Hy-Vee Grocery Store) Sections: Two sections, U1200 and Open. Players with ratings U1200, along with Unrated players, may register for either the U1200 or Open section. Requirements: Current memberships in both the United States Chess Federation and the SDCA (USCF membership registrations available online or at the site. SDCA membership at the site). Registration and Entry Fees : Registration available either online ( https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8211 ) or starting at 7:30 AM, at the tournament site. Fees--$40 if completed online on or before 3/1, $45 if completed online between 3/2 and 3/20, $50 if done at the tournament site on 3/21. Tournament Director: Waylon Lowe email: Click here to show mail address Time Controls: game in 90 minutes/30 sec increments (G90+30) Byes: A maximum of two byes (1/2 point each) will be granted if requested at least one day prior to the day(s) of the match(s). Prizes: Prizes: 1st-$100, 2nd-$50, 3rd-$25, 1st Scholastic-$50, U2000-$50, U1800-$50, U1600-$50, U1400-$50, U1200-$50 and Unrated-$25 (Prize money assumes 42 tournament players). Trophies will be given to the top three Open finishers, the top Scholastic player, as well as to both the top scoring Open and Scholastic individuals that are also Sioux Falls residents. Along with trophies, those two top scoring Sioux Falls residents will also be respectively bestowed with the titles of “Sioux Falls City Champion” and “Sioux Falls Scholastic City Champion”. Trophies will also be given to the highest scoring individual in each bracket. In case of ties, the trophy winners will be determined by standard USCF tie-break methods, as calculated in CaissaChess software. The methods, in order of precedent, will be Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, and Opposition’s Cumulative. Prize money will be divided equally among the tied winners. Additional Rules and Notes: Cellular phones and electronic devices are prohibited from use during the chess match. Please turn off all cellular phones and place in the center of the table (face-down) during tournament play. Other USCF rules will be followed during the tournament. Equipment: Please bring chess sets and clocks. Reservation link: State Scholastic Baymont K-12 TEAM VARSITY FORMAT : 5-Round team Swiss tournament with 4 players per team and one optional alternate. A match is won by the team scoring the most game points (2.5 points or more out of 4 games). Varsity I Division is Open to teams with any average rating. Varsity II Division is open to teams with an average team rating of less than 1100. Teams will be seeded based on a team rating derived from the rating average of the four players. Players must play in rating order except that the players within 50 rating points of each other may permanently switch positions prior to round one. Unrated players can play on any board. In calculating the average team rating, an unrated on board four is assigned 50 points below the rating of board three. An unrated on board three is assigned the average of the board two and four ratings. An unrated on board two is assigned the average of the board one and three ratings. An unrated on board one is assigned 50 points above the rating of board two. Schools may enter multiple teams in either section. No club teams are allowed. Players of all abilities are encouraged to participate. This is not a US Chess rated event. ELIGIBILITY and TEAM COMPOSITION: Only Wisconsin students are eligible. All K-12 Varsity teams must be composed entirely of 9th through 12th graders OR 8th graders and below. All players must be full-time students from the same school that holds classes during week days. If a high school does not have a 9th grade, then they may tap 9th graders from eligible feeder schools. Students in grades K-8 may play as a team in K-12 Team Varsity sections if from the same school. A home school or virtual school student may play on either a public or private school team. To play on a public school team, the student must live within the attendance boundary (not district) from which that public school draws. Any private school seeking to have these students on their team must use the same public school attendance boundary in which their school building is located. Players from outside their boundaries are not allowed to play on that school’s team. Home-schooled students are considered to be in 9th grade when they are 14 as of September 1st of the school year. Players must be under the age of 19 as of September 1st of the school year. RATINGS : March rating supplement will be used. Tournament Directors can choose the highest of the US Chess ratings (regular, quick, live, online) for pairing purposes only. Ratings are not affected by this event. SCHEDULE: Round 1 Saturday at 10:00am Round 2 Saturday at 1:00pm Round 3 Saturday at 4:00pm Round 4 Sunday at 9:30am Round 5 Sunday at 12:30pm Awards Sunday at 3:30pm or earlier The time control is Game in 60 minutes with a 5-second delay. Accelerated pairings may be used for the first two rounds. Boards, sets, and clocks are provided. PRIZES : Trophies/Plaques will be awarded to the top eight Division I teams and top eight Division II teams, first place team members, their coach, and each board champion. If a tie for 1st place in Division I exists, a blitz playoff will determine the State Champion. Every participant is eligible for an additional award (medal, chocolate or fruit leather). TIEBREAKS : US Amateur Team tiebreaks will be used as a primary tiebreak for team standings (if needed, the order of additional tiebreaks is Solkoff, Cumulative Opposition, Cumulative, and Modified Median). For board prizes, every person involved in a tie will receive a prize. ENTRY FEE : $160 per team. Varsity teams need to register by March 4th. If you are unsure about the exact roster, please register your team(s) by emailing the organizers. All rosters must be finalized by 8:00am of March 21st. This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address ! Gilligan's Bar and Grill Monday, March 23, 2026 Event Overview Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.) Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level. Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad. We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings. Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads. Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament. Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Sunday, March 29, 2026 Event Overview Join the 2025-26 CalChess Super States K & K-5 Championship and other K-12 sections for a high-level weekend of friendly chess competition! This is the greatest opportunity for scholastic players to earn state-level recognition in a supportive competitive environment, as well as to earn personal trophies. Register here You must log in or sign up before you can register. Online registration closes at 12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament. Onsite registration is subject to availability ($44 additional fee incurred). Late fees applied starting March 21 or when reaching capacity. Sections Players will need to register based on their 2025-26 school grade and their March Supplement Rating (i.e., rating as of Feb. 19) into one of the following sections: K-12 Rookie (unr.) K-12 Beginner (100-399) K-5 Jr. Varsity (400-799) K-12 Intermediate (400-799) 6-12 Jr. Varsity (800+) KG Champ (400+) K-5 Champ (800+) 6-12 Advanced (800+) Play-up rule A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is NOT allowed. Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up. (Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their March USChess Published Supplement Rating) Schedule K-5 Jr. Varsity, K-12 Rookie, K-12 Beginner & K-12 Intermediate: Time Control: 5x G/25 d5 Two schedules available: Saturday OR Sunday Round Times: Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. OR Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. 6-12 Jr. Varsity: Time Control: 5x G/25 d5 Round Times: Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. KG Champ: Time Control: 5x G/25 d5 Round Times: Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. K-5 Champ & 6-12 Advanced: Time Control: 6x G/65 d5 Round Times: Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m. Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m. ½-point bye is available for ONE (1) round, except for the last round (Byes must be requested at least 30 min before that round's start). 0-point byes are available for any round. If you request more than one bye, we will give you a ½-point for the latest round possible except for the last round (0-point byes for all other rounds). Awards Personal Trophies to all players with a winning record. One trophy per player. Trophy size vary based on standings. Medals to all other players. Team Trophies to all of the following with two or more players in all sections combined: Clubs Schools A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for awards. Fees Entry fee: K-5 Champ and 6-12 Advanced: $113 All other sections: $79 Play up fee: +$29 Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ). Late fees, starting: Mar. 22: +$11 Mar. 24: +$22 Mar. 26: +$33 Onsite fee: +$44 BayAreaChess Membership discounts are NOT redeemable for late and onsite fees. Withdrawals Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions: until Mar. 21, 4% processing fee. from Mar. 22 to Mar. 23, $11 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee. from Mar. 24 to Mar. 25, $22 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee. from Mar. 26 onward, NO REFUND will be issued. Only withdrawals made before or on Mar. 25 are eligible for refund. Change requests After registration, changes can be requested at bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees: until Mar. 26, $7 change fee. on Mar. 27, $15 change fee. The following requests are exempt from the change fee: playing up to a higher section. requesting byes. updating club and/or school. Other requirements USCF membership must be active. More info available here . Acosta Email: [email protected] Phone: (281) 844 4139 Pricing Early Registration: $32, ends on March 1, 2026 Regular Registration: $37, between March 16-22, 2026 Late Registration: $40, between , March 23-26, 2026 Active USCF membership is required by February 15, 2026. Visit new.uschess.org/join-us-chess starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership! Visit chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals! TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee. Visit texaschess.org/memberships to join TCA or renew your membership! Pricing is included in the registration form automatically. Eligibility Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties: Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list Sections High School Open: Any High Schooler may enter this section. High School U1000: Only High Schoolers rated 1000 or below may enter this section. Girls Open: Any Young Lady from Grade K-12 Girls U1000: Any Young Lady Under 1000 Note: Sections may be combined in case of low registrations. Definitions: High School - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9. Middle School - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them. Elementary - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School. A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School. Primary - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5. K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12. Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve. Note: Sections are based on USCF January 2025 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will not determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament. Tournament Format Rounds: Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5). Membership: USCF and TCA memberships required. Rules: USCF rules apply. Open sections require notation and clocks (if available). Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25. Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks. Touch-move / Touch-take: Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed. Equipment: Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude! Every player needs to bring their clocks! Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID. Chess sets for the whole tournament will be provided! Schedule No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at before 11:59pm on March 26, 2026. Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play. Round 1: Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination. Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Thursday March 26th, 2026 at 7pm. Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm. Teams Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association. Team members must attend the same school campus full-time or belong to the same Home School Association . Sections are not combined for teams. Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team. Awards Trophies: Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section. 1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th . Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy. Tie Breaks: Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard) We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio on March 28, 2026 for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess! benefit and encourage both new and experienced players. MONTHLY SPECIAL PROMOTIONS & ANNOUNCEMENTS: Always FREE registration for players with current USCF rating over 2000! Entry fee deducted from winnings. SPECIAL AWARD: Check registration form for details 2025-2026 SEASON SPECIAL PROJECTS, CONTESTS & SPECIAL RECOGNITIONS: 2025-2026 Brilliancy Award - Throughout the 2025-2026 season, players may submit notation to report their, or their opponent's, most brilliant moves! The notation must be legible, clearly labeled with player names, and the brilliant move must be marked. All submissions will be reviewed, and the player with the most brilliant move this season will receive an award at the May Open! SUBMISSIONS DUE BY APRIL 30. 2025-2026 Texas Chess Association Region I Recognition Program (Details are to be determined) - Categories and nomination procedures will be announced in the spring. You'll be able to make nominations; self-nomination will not be allowed. Winners must be TCA members. Awards will be presented at the May Open! SUBMISSIONS DUE BY APRIL 30. DATE: Saturday, March 28, 2026 LOCATION: Mad Hatter's House of Games; 1507 Texas Ave., Lubbock, TX 79401 START TIME: Round 1 begins at 11 AM (Players registered in advance online arrive to pay and check-in before 10:45; Players registering onsite arrive before 10:30am) ***NOTE: If you have not checked in by 10:45 you may receive a round 1 bye. END TIME: Most sections will finish at approximately 5:30 PM. The Novice Sections will finish at approximately 4:30 PM if players use full time allowed, but usually end earlier. Section awards will be presented shortly after all players in a section have completed their final round. Lower sections typically wrap up earlier than higher sections. COST: FREE REGISTRATION for players with current USCF rating over 2000 (entry fee deducted from winnings); $16/player for Early (Online at https://forms.gle/Uaj9FQctxt5TD73B7 ) or $21/player for Late (On-site) registration. Payment options include PayPal at the time of online registration or cash on-site at the door. ***There is a $1 cash payment discount, bringing cash payments down to $15 for early registration or $20 for onsite registration.*** REGISTRATION DEADLINES: Early (Online at https://forms.gle/Uaj9FQctxt5TD73B7 ) pre-registrations are due by 6 PM Friday, March 27, 2026. Late (On-site) registrations must be done between 10:00 and 10:30 AM on Saturday, March 28, 2026. TOURNAMENT DETAILS: Tournament Director: Robert Moore, Region I Director – Texas Chess Association USCF Rated Event: Current USCF membership required - PLEASE update your membership prior to tournament day. Contact us if you need help registering or renewing your USCF membership. Schedule: This is a swiss style tournament; See below for number of rounds and time controls for each section. Pairings will be posted 5 minutes after the last game in the previous round ends, and the new round will begin 10 minutes after the previous round is complete. This effectively adds a 10-minute break for players who are the last to finish a round. Round 1 begins promptly at 11 AM; if you are not checked in by 10:45, you may receive a round 1 bye. Equipment: Chess sets and notation supplies will be provided. Some chess clocks will be available, but please bring your own clock if you have one . Five sections as follows: Open Championship - Must be rated above 1300. If fewer than 8 players are above 1300, highest rated players below 1300 will be used to ensure at least 8 players in the section; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5 Reserve A (U1300) - Rating between 950 and 1300 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5 Reserve B (U1000) - Rating between 750 and 1000 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5 Novice A (U800) - Rating between 350 and 800 and unrated scholastic players; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5 Novice B (U400) - Rating under 400 and unrated players 5th grade or below; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5 EXCEPTIONS FOR PROVISIONALLY RATED PLAYERS : Adult players with provisional ratings below 750 may choose to play up into a Reserve section, but they may also register for the novice section that matches their provisional rating. Scholastic players with provisional ratings may be placed in an appropriate section by the tournament director. NOTE ABOUT PLAYERS' SECTION PLACEMENT: At the TD's discretion, sections may be added, deleted, or combined. A player near the rating cut-off may be moved to maintain an even number of players in as many sections as possible. Also, at the TD's discretion, section rating ranges may be revised onsite based on natural breaks in rating distributions, which could increase the number of players in the Open Championship section to more than 8. RATING DETERMINATION: USCF ratings as of March 23 will be used to determine section eligibility for this event. Prizes: Cash prizes for Open Championship and Reserve Sections: Cash prize guarantees are based on 50 registered players . The total guaranteed prize fund for 50 players is $350. The available cash prize fund will be increased or decreased based on registration variance from 50 players. At 100 players, the prize fund will grow to $1000! If there are fewer than 50 players, prizes may be given for fewer than 3 places in each section. Ties will follow USCF rules for splitting cash prizes. Trophies & medals for Novice sections: Trophies will be awarded to the top three finishers in each Novice section. Medals will be awarded to players who tie for third but do not receive a trophy. Standard tie breaks will be used. PHOTOGRAPHY: Photos may be taken during the tournament and awards ceremony. These images may be shared with Texas Chess Association, news outlets, or other interested groups or individuals. Images may be used for promotion of subsequent chess events. CONTACT: Completing the registration form linked below should generate an email to the address used to complete the form. Prior to the tournament, another email communication will be sent with a link to check tournament registration details. The top Kentucky player who has not already qualified will receive an invitation to this event. US Chess Membership is REQUIRED. All US Chess rules will be followed. Membership must be current through March 2026 Membership will NOT be available onsite, sign up at uschess.org Please bring membership ID number to the tournament Notation is required for all players. Players 8 years old or younger (or their parents) can ask tournament director before Round 1 for an exemption. Players younger than high school age (~14) must be accompanied by an adult. FORMAT Two Sections: both will be 4 Rounds - Swiss System OPEN Section: open to all USCF players and any rating level U1500 Section: open to USCF players with ratings below 1500 (unrated to 1499) G30;d5 (clocks will be set to 30 minutes per player, 5 second delay) Note: we reserve the right to have only one OPEN section if there is a low turnout the day of the tournament. SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport 22595 Shaw Road, Sterling, VA 20166 Saturday, March 28, 2026 at 9 am Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8461 Note about special rules for pairings: This tournament will feature Monrad pairings, which is a variation on Swiss pairings that reduces mismatches. The use of Monrad pairings eliminates the need for multiple sections as players are often paired against closely related opponents, especially in early rounds. To read more about Monrad Swiss pairings, visit Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss-system_tournament#Monrad_system Because we are using Monrad pairings, which are better at reducing mismatches, there are no separate K-3, K-5, K-8, and K-12 sections. Instead, there is just one section for everyone. To be eligible for grade-based prizes, please include the player's grade in the "grade" field when you register. Advantages of Monrad Pairings: Fewer mismatches, more games against closely-rated opponents Eliminate need for multiple sections Anyone can win the tournament (lower-rated players are more likely to play each other, which means that anyone has a chance to win) Less playing down (higher-rated players are less likely to have to play down) Tournament Information​ Four rounds: first round at 9 am, subsequent rounds occur as soon as possible One section: Monrad pairings reduce mismatches, eliminating the need for separate K-3, K-5, K-8, and K-12 sections (see note above) Time control: Game in 25 minutes with a 5-second delay ( US Chess regular and quick rated) Prizes: trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in each section Entry fee: $35 by 3/16, $40 by 3/23, $45 by 3/27, $50 by 3/28 (on-site registration closes 30 minutes before round 1) Boards and pieces will be provided for all players, but we don’t have enough clocks for everyone (those who have clocks are welcome to bring them) This tournament is US Chess rated, so an active US Chess membership is required. Click here to join the US Chess Federation for the first time or to renew an inactive membership: https://new.uschess.org/user/login?destination=/form/membership Don’t hesitate to reach out to us at Click here to show mail address with any questions Venue Information/Logistics PARKING: The hotel has free parking on the street. In the event that street parking is full, the hotel also has a garage. Chess players can park for a special rate of $5 in the garage. Free water will be provided for attendees. There is no scheduled lunch break, but there is almost always time for players to have food between games. There aren't any scheduled round times--rounds will occur as soon as possible. Time control: Game in 95 minutes with a 10-second increment. Only open to adults (18+). No exceptions. Round times: Saturday at 2 pm, Saturday at 6:30 pm, Sunday at 9 am, Sunday at 1 pm Later start on Saturday and earlier finish on Sunday allows players to drive to this tournament who live several hours away. Entry fee: $58 by 3/15, $65 by 3/21, $70 by 3/27, $75 on the day of the tournament. National masters will current ratings over 2200 play for free ($58 entry deducted from prizes). Email [email protected] to register for free as a 2200+ rated player. Three Sections: Premier (also FIDE rated), Under 1800, and Under 1400. Note: Players may not play up more than 100 points. A player may use either their live (unpublished) or published rating to qualify for a higher section. Players may also use their FIDE rating to qualify for a higher section. In the event that a player uses their live rating (or FIDE rating) to qualify for a higher section, this rating will also be used for pairings. Forfeit policy: A player who is more than thirty minutes late can be forfeited. PRIZES: $200 for 1st, $100 for 2nd in Premier; $100 for 1st in U1800, $100 for 1st in Under 1400; Top senior overall in the tournament (50+) prize of $100 (includes $50 donated to this prize from last year's winner). (Note that the top senior prize is accross all sections and is calculated completely separately from the other prizes. It is possible for a player to win the top senior prize in addition to another prize.) Up to two half-point byes are allowed. Half-point byes can be requested for any round. The deadline to request a half-point bye is prior to the start of round 3. We will have enough chess sets for all players, but clocks will not be provided for everyone. If you have a clock, please bring one. There is plenty of free parking at the playing venue. For questions, please email us at Click here to show mail address or call us at 703-609-0499. USCF membership required in all sections. This tournament is an Iowa State Chess Association Grand Prix points Mini-Qualifier in the Open section. Open: $35 online in advance or $40 cash-only in-person same day Reserve: $25 online in advance or $30 cash-only in-person same day Beginner/Youth: $20 online in advance or $25 cash-only in-person same day Register online at https://www.kingregistration.com/event/QuadCityMarchMadness2026 Sections & Time Controls: Open: 4-Round Swiss, G/65, d5 Reserve (under 1400): 4-Round Swiss, G/60, d5 Beginner/Youth (under 800): 4-Round Swiss, G/20, d0 ♟️♟️♟️ Open & Reserve Section Rounds: 1st round: 10:00am Lunch Break - Pizza and Drinks included with registration fee 2nd round: 1:30pm 3rd round: 4:00pm 4th round: 6:30pm *Rounds may start earlier if prior round has been completed and if all players are in agreement. Beginner/Youth Section Rounds: 1st round: 10:00am and then Rounds 2-4 ASAP there after with Lunch break approximately between 3rd & 4th rounds ♟️♟️♟️ Prizes: Open Section: 1st Place: $150 ; 2nd Place: $100 ; 3rd Place: $75 ; 4th Place: $50 Reserve Section (under 1400): 1st Place: $100 ; 2nd Place: $75 ; 3rd Place: $50 Beginner/Youth Section (under 800): Trophies for 1st - 5th Place ; 6th - 20th Place will receive participation medals. ♟️♟️♟️ Additional info: US Chess Federation (USCF) membership required. On Site Registration Available. $3 off for adults, young adults and students if you register through our affiliation. Parents/Guardians of young chess players are responsible for their children. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or coffee in waiting area while games are in progress. Boards and clocks will ONLY be provided for the Beginner/Youth section games. Open and Reserve section players must bring their own regulated clock and board (dimensions listed below). Notation of moves on scoresheet is mandatory for Open and Reserve sections games. Scoresheets will be provided. No electronic scoresheets allowed. By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well. ♟️♟️♟️ For questions: Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890 ♟️♟️♟️ Tournament Directors: Gary Nordick & Mariela Treviño ♟️♟️♟️ Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette: Scoresheets: Notation of moves in Open and Reserve sections is required. Players must record moves in algebraic notation, typically writing the move after executing it on the board. Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute. Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible. One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock. Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically. Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent). Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand. "J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it. Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square. No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play. Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be courteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen. Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe. Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent. USCF Board Regulations & Features: Square Size: 2.25 inches is standard, though 2 to 2.5 inches is permissible. Overall Size: 20" x 20" or 22" x 22" (approx. 50-55 cm). Material: Usually flexible vinyl, often featuring algebraic notation on all sides. Proportion Requirement: The King's base diameter should occupy roughly 75% to 80% of the square size. Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section. ♟️♟️♟️ Western Illinois Chess Club Mission Statement: To strengthen our community by bringing people together through providing opportunities for chess education, fostering respect, collaboration, and mutual growth. International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 ) Tournament Purpose This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026. Date & Time Round 1 starts on March 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM . Venue Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009. Time Control G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move). Format 6-round Swiss system. Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions). Ratings This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official April 2026 USCF ratings will be used. Byes Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration. No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes . A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round. Entry Fee $60 – Until February 28, 2025, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first. $80 – Until March 14, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first. $100 – Until March 29, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled. Cancellation & Refund Policy A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by March 25, 2025, at 12:00 AM (midnight) . No refunds will be issued after this deadline. Withdrawal Policy Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw. Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC. Number of Entries Maximum of 64 participants. Eligibility Open to all players with active USCF membership . Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1. Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee. Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes. Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie . Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before April 5, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize. Tiebreaks Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods : Solkoff Modified Median Cumulative If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner. Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) . Monday, May 11, 2026 Event Overview MSJE 2026 Qingming to Lixia Monday Night Marathon is a USCF-rated tournament for all members of MSJE Chess community. Qingming 清明, also known as Clear and Bright, is the 5th of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar. Guyu 谷雨, also known as Grain Rain, is the 6th of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar. Lixia 立夏, also known as Start of Summer, is the 7th of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar. Zero-point bye/withdraw has to be requested before the section pairing is done. Withdrawals: Withdrawals can be requested 1 week before the tournament start date. Refunds will incur a $15 processing and transaction fee. NO REFUNDS/NO CREDITS after March 27, 2026 and NO EXCEPTION. More Details: March US Chess ratings and rules will be used for pairings and awarding prizes. FIDE Laws of Chess apply to FIDE rated sections; US Chess rules apply to other sections Unrated players will be placed at TD’s discretion. Foreign players must disclose FIDE ID, foreign ratings or online ratings before round one is paired. Failure to disclose playing history may result in forfeiture and withdrawal from the event. USA players without a FIDE ID and playing in FIDE rated sections must obtain a FIDE ID from US Chess or must disclose city, state, email, date of birth and agree to receive a USA FIDE ID. No Spectators allowed in tournament area. All non-essential communication devices must be powered off completely while inside the playing hall (not just on silent) and must remain in the player’s bag or face up on the table. Devices must remain at the board during game play. Penalties up to or including loss of game and removal from the tournament for violations of this policy. Only FIDE and US Chess approved electronic notation devices are allowed; players in FIDE sections must email (PGN) game files to the organizer. Duplicate scoresheets required in FIDE sections. Notation required for all sections and must continue for the entire game. Per rules, moves must be made on the board before recording them and the king must be moved first when castling. Please bring your own clock . Boards and sets will be provided. Only snacks and drinks allowed at the chess board. All other food must remain outside the playing room. Default late forfeiture time is one hour. TD may extend this time at TD’s discretion. PLAYING UP: If you are rated U1900 but are at least 1700 you may play up into the Championship section for $35. PRIZE FUND $2,500 - 1st place in each section is guaranteed . 2nd place and 3rd place 25% OF ENTRY FEES B/50 in all sections combined. 15% BONUS FOR CLUB MEMBERS . Championship 1st $800 ; Challengers 1st $550 . Un-rated may play in any section but are limited to winning $150 except in the top section where they are eligible for all prizes. DRAWS PRIOR TO 30 MOVES AND BOTH PLAYERS ARE INELIGIBLE FOR ANY PRIZE MONEY! ONLY MEMBERS OF POISON PAWNS CHESS CLUB ARE ONLY ELIGIBLE FOR 100% OF THE CASH PRIZES ! (So isn't it time you joined!) CLICK HERE TO BECOME A MEMBER CANCELLATION: You may cancel up to 72 hours before the beginning of Round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $25, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee IF USED WITHIN 30-DAYS OF ORIGINAL EVENT . BYES: One ½ point bye available, must be declared before the beginning of round 2. No last round byes except for zero point byes. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9. There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza . Several others are within walking distance. Plenty of FREE parking. April '26 Chess Tournament and League Columbia County Library, Room A Saturday, April 4, 2026 Event Overview Join the Columbia County Chess Association for our monthly chess tournament as a part of the year-long running Chess League. Each League Tournament will consist of 4 Rounds G/35;+5 games, Swiss style tournaments at the Columbia County Library with three sections; Open, U1300 and U800. Section Prizes are increased this year with $700 between the three sections (based on 20 Registrants). Compete in as many or as few Chess League events, earning points throughout the year. The top 12 players from each section will be invited to the Chess League round-robin tournament at the conclusion of the regular season to determine the Chess League Champion! Season Pass and Multi-month registration discounts available. Quad Format - No Prizes - All ratings welcome. $10 entry - cash only - Adults and Kids Welcome No Late Entries - No Byes - No Withdrawals ONSITE REGISTRATION ONLY US Chess Membership Required, will affect quick and regular rating. Location: 9:15 AM - Registration Begins 9:45 AM - Registration Ends (NO LATE ENTRIES) 10:00 AM - Round One 12:30 PM - Round Two 2:15 PM - Round Three What is Quad Format? Players are grouped in order of rating. The top four are grouped, then the next four are grouped, and so on. The groups (quads) of four play each other in a three-round round-robin. No late entries, no withdrawals . Quads are round robins. Please do not play if you can't stay for all three games. Leaving in the middle of a quad is rude and provides an extreme inconvenience to the other three players in your quad. Tournament April 4, 2026 12466 Los Indios Trail, Ste. 100 Austin, TX 78729 * USCF Membership Required * Free Parking Provided Capacity: 100 players Note that this is a scholastic event, only players who are 18 years of age or under can play in this tournament. All players will be divided into five sections: SECTION A: 1600+ USCF rated SECTION B: 1200 - 1599 USCF rated SECTION C: 800 - 1199 USCF rated SECTION D: 400 - 799 USCF rated SECTION E: Under 400 USCF rated or unrated **Players are not allowed to play up or down** ENTRY FEES: Early Bird: $40 before 11:59pm, March 15, 2026 Standard Fee: $50 before 11:59 March 29, 2026 Late Fee: $65 after March 30, 2026 PRIZES: Trophies for 1st Place, Medals for 2nd and 3rd Junior Qualifier Points: Top 10 places in Section A will earn points according to the following table: 1st Place: 25 JQ Points 2nd Place: 18 JQ Points 3rd Place: 15 JQ Points 4th Place: 12 JQ Points 5th Place: 10 JQ Points 6th Place: 8 JQ Points 7th Place: 6 JQ Points 8th Place: 4 JQ Points 9th Place: 2 JQ Points 10th Place: 1 JQ Points For more information about the point system, visit https://austin-chess.com/tournaments/ TIME CONTROL: Section A: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay) Section B: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay) Section C: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay) Section D: G/30, d5 (30 minutes per player with a 5-second delay) Section E: G/30, d5 (30 minutes per player with a 5-second delay) 4-Round Swiss System Schedule SECTIONS A and B: 1st round: 9:00 AM 2nd round: 11:15 PM Lunch Break: 1:30-2:30 PM 3rd round: 2:30 PM 4th round: 4:45 PM SECTION C: 1st round: 10:00 AM 2nd round: 11:45 AM Lunch Break: 1:30-2:30 PM 3rd round: 2:30 PM 4th round: 4:15 PM 5-Round Swiss System Schedule SECTIONS D and E: 1st round: 10:00 AM 2nd round: 11:15 AM 3rd round: 12:30 PM Lunch Break: 1:30 PM 4th round: 2:30 PM 5th round: 3:45 PM Closing ceremony: After the last game of the section finishes. Format: Round-Robin Total Rounds: 3 Round Times: 2 pm and Rounds 2 & 3 on a rolling schedule Time Control: G/30;+5 (Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second increment at each move.) Games will be US Chess regular & quick-rated (so called dual-rated). Players will be split into groups of four (quads) based on their ratings, from the highest-rated to the lowest-rated. In case the last quad is not four players, they will play a mini-3 round Swiss tournament with 5-7 players or they may play double round robin. Monthly supplemental OTB regular rating will be used. The Chief TD has discretion to use a player's USCF online rating (ONL) or live rating for pairing purposes in extreme cases where fairness will be preserved by doing so Minor roster shifts to avoid family member pairings may be possible No byes are available Forfeit time is 30 minutes WHEN April 4th , 2026 (Saturday) @ 2:00 PM Please arrive at the venue at least 10 minutes before the start time. WHERE ​Holiday Inn Express & Suites Gilbert near Mesa Gateway Airport 5530 S Power Road, Gilbert, AZ 85295, USA Intersection: Power Rd & E Ray Rd APPROXIMATE HOURS 2:00pm – 5:30pm Might end early based on the quad. Tallahassee and Challenger Learning Center (CLC) , the Tallahassee Young Knights (TYK) Chess Club is organizing a USCF-rated chess tournament in April 2026 at CLC, located in the heart of downtown The main event will be a four-round Quick tournament, along with a six-round Blitz side event. More details can be found at our CLC website and event page . Main Event: Quick Date: April 5th (Sunday), 2026 Location: Challenger Learning Center, 200 S Duval St, Tallahassee, FL 32301 Format: 4SS, G/20, d5 Sections: Open, U1400, U800 Check in: 9:30am (first game is expected to start at 10am sharp) Round Times: 10am-11am-1pm-2pm. Prizes: Open ($100 + trophy 1st, $80 2nd, $40 1st U1600), U1400 ($80 + trophy 1st, $60 2nd, $40 1st U1100), U800 ($80 + trophy 1st, $60 2nd) Side Event: Blitz Format: 6SS, G/3, inc 2 Section: Open Check in: 3:00pm Round Times: 1st round 3:30pm, ASAP thereafter. Prizes: $80 + trophy 1st, $60 2nd, $40 1st U1400, $40 1st U800 Notes: Active USCF membership is required. Championship on March 21, 2026 as well as Girls' Championship on April 11, 2026) Online Registration Only. $30 by April 4, 2026, $40 thereafter. Registration closes at 8:30 a.m. the morning of the tournament. All equipment provided. No check-in required: players not reporting to their first round game before their time expires will be withdrawn from the tournament. Please contact Click here to show mail address if there are any issues with your registration. Pairings and standings available in real time online, see "Pairings & Standings" in www.scscholastic.com menu. Active USCF membership required. Memberships can be purchased/renewed at uschess.org/join-us-chess . Register Now Format The Girls' Championship tournament is organized as a single-section (K-12) tournament, 5-Round Swiss G/30;d5. Schedule Round 1: 10:00 a.m. Round 2: 11:20 a.m. Round 3: 1:30 p.m. Round 4: 2:50 p.m. Round 5: 4:10 p.m. Awards: 5:40 p.m. Prizes Top 8 receive trophies. Superlative awards to youngest participant, best debut, and biggest upset. The SC Chess Association awards the first place finisher an invitation and a stipend to compete as the South Carolina representative to Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions . The WIM Ruth Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions is an annual invitational event run by US Chess that has determined the Haring National Champion since 2013 . A total of $18,700 in prizes will be awarded, including $5,800 in scholarship and cash prizes to the champion. The champion will also qualify for the U.S. Girls Junior Championship and either the World Youth Championship or the World Cadet Championships . The second place finisher in the SC Girls' Scholastic Championship is named the South Carolina Representative to the Susan Polgar Invitational Tournament in St. Louis, MO, and given a stipend for attendance. This "Hannah 'Tori' Whatley GRIT Award," started by the Whatley family in 2015, honors a young South Carolina female chess player chosen to compete at the Susan Polgar Girls Invitational. Named after Tori Whatley, the first South Carolinian girl to attend in 2008 as a 6th grader, it celebrates her tenacity. She competed six times, a rare feat, and was known for upsetting higher-rated players, like in her debut when she drew a player 518 points above her and beat Virginia’s champion. In 2012, she placed 22nd. Tori joined Webster University’s SPICE program in 2015, the only North American female on the team until 2018. After earning a studio art degree, she worked briefly at the World Chess Hall of Fame and now studies nuclear engineering at Florida International University. Sponsored by Tori and her dad David, a former scholastic chess coordinator, the award reflects their love for chess and aims to inspire others to pursue their passions. Please complete all your Quad games. WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad. ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!! This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address !
