Seniors Women menu arrow_back 2026 April Tournament Houston Chess Studio Sunday, April 12, 2026 Event Overview Organizer Azeri Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 ) Tournament Director International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 ) Tournament Purpose This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026. Date & Time Round 1 starts on April 12, 2026, at 10:00 AM . Venue Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009. Time Control G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move). Format 6-round Swiss system. Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions). Ratings This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official April 2026 USCF ratings will be used. Byes Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration. No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes . A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round. Entry Fee $60 – Until March 15, 2026, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first. $80 – Until April 1, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first. $100 – Until April 12, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled. Cancellation & Refund Policy A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by April 8, 2026, at 12:00 AM (midnight) . No refunds will be issued after this deadline. Withdrawal Policy Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw. Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC. Number of Entries Maximum of 64 participants. Eligibility Open to all players with active USCF membership . Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1. Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee. Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund . Tournament Schedule (Estimated Round Start Times) 1st Round – 10:00 AM 2nd Round – 11:25 AM 30-minute break 3rd Round – 1:20 PM 4th Round – 2:45 PM 5th Round – 4:05 PM 6th Round – 5:25 PM Closing Ceremony – 6:45 PM Prize Fund Prize distribution is based on the final number of players in the tournament: < 10 players 1st: $300 + plaque Total prize fund: $300 10–15 players 1st: $400 + plaque 2nd: $100 Total prize fund: $500 16–20 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 Total prize fund: $750 21–25 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 3rd: $150 Total prize fund: $900 26–30 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 3rd: $150 Best U1600: $150 Best U1200: $150 Total prize fund: $1,200 31–35 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 3rd: $150 Best U1600: $150 Best U1200: $150 Best U800: $150 Total prize fund: $1,350 36–40 players 1st: $550 + plaque 2nd: $350 3rd: $150 Best U1600: $150 Best U1400: $150 Best U1200: $150 Best U1000: $150 Best U800: $150 Total prize fund: $1,800 41–45 players 1st: $590 + plaque 2nd: $350 3rd: $210 Best U1600: $200 Best U1400: $200 Best U1200: $150 Best U1000: $150 Best U800: $150 Total prize fund: $2,000 46–50 players 1st: $590 + plaque 2nd: $410 3rd: $300 Best U1600: $200 Best U1400: $200 Best U1200: $200 Best U1000: $200 Best U800: $200 Total prize fund: $2,300 > 50 players 1st: $590 + plaque 2nd: $410 3rd: $300 Best U1600: $300 Best U1400: $300 Best U1200: $300 Best U1000: $300 Best U800: $300 Total prize fund: $2,800 If rating prizes are offered, unrated players are eligible only for prizes in the lowest rating group . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes. Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie . Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before April 19, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize. Tiebreaks Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods : Solkoff Modified Median Cumulative If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner. Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) . No electronic devices (phones, smartwatches, etc.) are allowed unless explicitly permitted by the arbiter for medical reasons . A designated storage box will be provided for electronic devices. Photography & Video Recording By registering, players consent to being photographed and recorded by the Tournament Director and their associates for promotional purposes. Equipment & Notation Rules Chess sets, clocks, scoresheets, and pens will be provided by the organizer. Notation is mandatory unless a player has less than 5 minutes remaining on their clock. Players may keep a yellow scoresheet copy and a pen . However, players are encouraged to bring an extra pen , as available pens may be limited . Parking & Nearby Restaurants: Free parking is available near the venue. 3 restaurants in the same strip center as venue: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza . Several others are within walking distance. Questions? Contact us at [email protected] . At-Risk-Youth Seniors Women menu arrow_back SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15) Sunday, April 12, 2026 Event Overview REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments! All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome. Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance. The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration. For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year). Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#). However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional. If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy! [If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.] Here are the details: Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door). Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm. 4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system. A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost. Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes. Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds. G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move. USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration. This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play. Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating. Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess. Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under). Want your child to "play up?" Just email Mike at [email protected] . Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections. There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month). Notation is required in the premiere sections. The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section. Casual Tournament: Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time. The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout. It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number). There will be four rounds. There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners! Other details: Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director. Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months). An outside playground is available. Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria. There is a guest WiFi network with password August27. The site is wheelchair accessible. Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function. Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available. Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids. If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough. Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections. In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen). Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify). Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament! Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link). Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . We hope to see you there! REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events Address: 6131 N Michigan Rd. Seniors Women menu arrow_back Tunnelvision XLIII Columbia Chess Club Saturday, April 18, 2026 Event Overview The Columbia Chess Club Presents Columbia Tunnelvision XLIII April 18, 2026 $1000 Guaranteed 10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5 Columbia Chess Club 6169 St. Andrews Rd. Columbia, SC 29212 Register Registration Standard registration is $40 until the day before the tournament. $50 late registration the day before/morning of. Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players. Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout. Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players . Register Now Pre-Registered Players Format 4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess. Live Standings/Pairings/Boards The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links. Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below. Live Standings Prizes $1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed. Championship (1600+) $400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70 Under 1600 $300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50 Under 1000 $300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50 Schedule Round 1: 10:30 a.m. Round 2: 12:50 p.m. Round 3: 2:40 p.m. Round 4: 4:30 p.m. Byes A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round. The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances. Location Columbia Chess Club 6169 St. Andrews Rd., Ste A Columbia, SC 29212 Questions? Email [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938. Parking The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking. Food The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks. By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament. Many other restaurants are available close by! Sunday, April 19, 2026 Event Overview Register at chessacademy.com/tournaments ! The official Maryland State Scholastic Championship tournament and Denker, Barber, Rockefeller, and Ashley Qualifiers! With special guest IM Danny Rensch, who will be doing a lecture and book signing of his memoir Dark Squares at 11am on Saturday This is a US Chess rated Swiss style tournament. There are ten different sections for players depending on their age and skill. Sections include K-1 U-400, PS U-600, ES U-800, MS U-1000, HS U-1200, K-1 Champ, PS Champ (550+), ES Champ (750+), MS Champ (950+), and HS Champ (1150+). Participants play only against opponents in their own section. Under sections for elementary school, K-1 Champ, and PS Champ will play all their games on Saturday. Under sections for middle and high school will play all their games on Sunday. ES Champ, MS Champ, and HS Champ will play their games on Saturday and Sunday. Championship sections are only open to students who live in or attend school in MD, under sections are open to participants from any state. All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all five rounds. We provide FREE US Chess Federation memberships for all participants, a $24 value! For players using chess clocks, the time control is G/25 with a 5-second time delay. For ES, MS, and HS championship sections, the time control is G/75 d5. Trophies to the top players and teams in each section. Prices increase $10 at noon on Tuesday, 3/31 and $10 at noon on Tuesday, 4/14. Questions? PETERSBURG EXTRA QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT G60; d5. Saint Petersburg Chess Club Saturday, April 18, 2026 Event Overview There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games. WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list. The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad. ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!! Center Saturday, April 18, 2026 - Sunday, April 19, 2026 Event Overview Compete in the 2025-26 CalChess Super States K-3 & K-8 Championship and other K-12 sections, where scholastic players enjoy exciting games at a state-level championship! It's the perfect opportunity to gain experience and earn trophies. Register here You must log in or sign up before you can register. Online registration closes at 12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament. Onsite registration is subject to availability ($44 additional fee incurred). Late fees applied starting April 12 or when reaching capacity. Sections Players will need to register based on their 2025-26 school grade and their April Supplement Rating (i.e., rating as of Mar. 19) into one of the following sections: K-12 Rookie (unr.) K-12 Beginner (100-399) K-3 Jr. Varsity (400-799) 4-12 Intermediate (400-799) K-12 Intermediate (400-799) 4-12 Advanced (800-1199) K-12 Advanced (800-1199) K-8 Jr. Varsity (800-1199) K-3 Champ (800+) K-8 Champ (1200+) 9-12 Advanced (1200+) Play-up rule A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is NOT allowed. Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up. (Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their April USChess Published Supplement Rating) Schedule K-12 Rookie & K-12 Beginner : Time Control: 5x G/25 d5 Two schedules available: Saturday OR Sunday Round Times: Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. OR Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. K-3 Jr. Varsity , 4-12 Intermediate & K-12 Advanced : Time Control: 5x G/25 d5 Round Times: Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. K-3 Champ , K-12 Intermediate & 4-12 Advanced : Time Control: 5x G/25 d5 Round Times: Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m. K-8 Jr. Varsity , K-8 Champ & 9-12 Advanced : Time Control: 6x G/65 d5 Round Times: Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m. Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m. ½-point bye is available for ONE (1) round, except for the last round (Byes must be requested at least 30 min before that round's start). 0-point byes are available for any round. If you request more than one bye, we will give you a ½-point for the latest round possible except for the last round (0-point byes for all other rounds). Awards Personal Trophies to all players with a winning record. One trophy per player. Trophy size vary based on standings. Medals to all other players. Team Trophies to all of the following with two or more players in all sections combined: Clubs Schools A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for awards. Fees Entry fee: K-8 Jr. Varsity, K-8 Champ and 9-12 Advanced: $113 All other sections: $79 Play up fee: +$29 Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ). Late fees, starting: Apr. 12: +$11 Apr. 14: +$22 Apr. 16: +$33 Onsite fee: +$44 BayAreaChess Membership discounts are NOT redeemable for late and onsite fees. Withdrawals Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions: until Apr. 11, 4% processing fee. from Apr. 12 to Mar. 13, $11 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee. from Apr. 14 to Mar. 15, $22 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee. from Apr. 16 onward, NO REFUND will be issued. Only withdrawals made before or on Apr. 15 are eligible for refund. Change requests After registration, changes can be requested at bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees: until Apr. 16, $7 change fee. on Apr. 17, $15 change fee. The following requests are exempt from the change fee: playing up to a higher section. requesting byes. updating club and/or school. Other requirements USCF membership must be active. More info available here . Total prize fund b/60 with 50% guaranteed. Class prizes: Class prizes to be determined by official April USCF rating. Unrated players are eligible for class and section prizes in the open section. Eligibility: $60 early entry fee if purchased one week prior. $70 standard entry fee if purchased two days prior. $80 late and same-day entry fee. Capacity limited to the first 120 players, please pre-register to guarantee your spot. Current USCF membership required. Free FIDE membership available to all players in top section with valid USCF membership. Ratings: If a player does not have a regular rating, the highest of their quick and blitz will be used. 100 elo added to provisional ratings. Unrated players should report to the tournament directors so they may attempt to assign a rating for pairing and prize purposes. Unrated players may play in the open section or the U1500 section, but will only be eligible for the open section place prizes unless the tournament directors have been able to assign a rating. For unrated USCF players with established foreign ratings, the most current USCF conversion will be used (with preference toward their FIDE rating, if available). Games including FIDE rated players 2400 or above are not FIDE rated due to time control and format. Byes: Two half point byes are available upon request. No bye requests shall be made after round three other than for emergency situations. Parking: Parking permits are not required in most parking zones on Tulane University campus during the weekend. For ease, we recommend using the Diboll Garage. Diboll Garage is a short walk from the Lavin-Bernick Center and has plenty of space available for our attendees. Consult the annotated parking map here . Hotel info: We recommend the St Charles Inn - Superior Hotel. We do not have a group rate, however. Late players: Any player arriving at the chessboard more than 30 minutes late from the actual starting time of the round will lose their game (xref USCF 13D and FIDE 6.7.1). If both players arrive late elapsed time will be split between the players (xref USCF 16K and FIDE 6.7.2). Prize payouts: Players have 10 days after the conclusion of the tournament to claim their prize. We will email you twice. Please check your email if you believe you are prize eligible. STATE CHAMPIONSHIP A TCA GRAND PRIX EVENT! Registration: https://www.kingregistration.com/event/2026QuickChessChamp 9 rounds of G/15 (no delay no increment) on Saturday April 25th. One section. USCF rated for Quick Chess only. This tournament will not affect your regular rating. Keeping score (notation) is not required in Quick Chess! QUALIFICATIONS : All chess players, regardless of residence, are welcome as long as they meet the membership requirements. You must have an unexpired USCF and Texas Chess Association membership in good standing on the day of the tournament . Please note, however, that while residents of other states may participate, and win cash prizes, state champion titles are for Texas residents only . BYES : Every player is entitled to a single half-point bye if requested before the beginning of round 1. After that time, all requested byes will be for zero points. All last round byes are zero point byes. SECTIONS: Just one open section. The April Rating Supplement will be used for pairings and for determination of the Class State Championship certificates. SCHEDULE : Round 1 at 10am, others ASAP, one hour lunch break from about noon to 1. Last round should end about 4 or 4:30. CAPACITY: Limited to 72, so register early, it might sell out. It is a State Championship event after all. ENTRY FEES : $45 by April 4th, $55 by April 22nd, $65 thereafter. Poison Pawn members use your $10 off coupon. GM's & IMs enter free, entry fee deducted from any prize won. CANCELLATION : You may cancel up to 24 hours before the beginning of round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $15, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee. PRIZES : Overall 1st place - the title of "2026 Texas Quick Chess State Champion", a trophy, and $250 guaranteed . Overall 2nd place $175, and overall 3rd place $100. 2nd & 3rd place based on 25 paid entries. All 3 cash prizes increased proportionally with more than 25 entries. (last year's prize fund was $380/$270/$160 with 49 entries). All cash prizes paid via PayPal. In case of a tie for first place the trophy will be awarded using standard USCF tiebreakers: Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, Cumulative Opponent's score. No tie breaks , if 2 or more tie for top score in a class they will each get a certificate declaring them the "2026 Texas Quick Chess State Co-Champion" of that Class! Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9. Also within a mile is the Heights House Hotel , an America’s Best Value , and a Luxury Inn . Google them for info. WHERE: THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO , is dedicated to providing a quality, high tech, chess playing experience for players of all levels, and their parents. Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009. Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45. There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza. Several others are within walking distance. Plenty of FREE parking. Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive. End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00. The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time. Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play. Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king). Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.) Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections. The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission. Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership. Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment. Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack. Registration: The registration fee is $30. Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event. Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts. Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal. For more information: Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720). Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Eureka College Saturday, April 25, 2026 Event Overview Event Overview Saturday April 25, 2026 Cerf Center S Burgess St. Eureka, IL 61530 US Chess Membership is Required for Open and U1401 sections. All US Chess Rules will be followed. Notation is required in all rated sections. Players 8 years old or younger (or their parents) can ask the tournament director before Round 1 for an exemption, if they are still learning to write in general. Players and spectators younger than high school age (~14) must be accompanied by an adult. The accompanying adult must be present at the tournament site. Disruptive and/or destructive behavior will result in dismissal from the tournament and site. Players are responsible for the behavior of anyone accompanying them to the tournament. Three Sections: Open - Open to all players. Active US Chess membership required. U1401 - Players must have a published USCF Regular Rating below 1401. Unrated players may play in this section, however they are only eligible for place prizes. Active US Chess membership required. Non-rated - Geared towards players who would like to try out tournament chess before committing to a US Chess membership. Notation not required for this section. US Chess membership not required. Check your rating here: https://ratings.uschess.org/ USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for section eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating. Format: Open and U1401 Sections 4 Rounds SS; G/40+10 (Clocks will be set with 40 minutes per player, and a 10 second increment that adds back after each move) Non-rated Section 4 Rounds SS; G/20+5 (Clocks will be set with 20 minutes per player, and a 5 second increment that adds back after each move) Entry Fees: Entry Fees will be paid onsite with cash only. General Entry Fee for Open and U1401 Sections: $30 Players with a US Chess Regular Rating 1800 or higher (using published or most recent live rating): $15 Players with a US Chess Regular Rating 2200 or higher (using published or most recent live rating): Free General Entry Fee for Non-rated Section: $10 *Eureka College Students, Staff, and Faculty will receive free entry to any section. **If a live rating is used for a discounted entry fee, that rating will be used for prize and pairing purposes. Pre-registration link: https://forms.gle/EcjG5QydNEm448so6 Prizes Prizes for Open and U1401 sections are based on 30 paid entries in rated sections. Open 1st - $150 2nd - $90 Top U2001/Unrated - $60 Top U1701/Unrated - $50 U1401 1st - $100 2nd - $60 Top U1201 - $40 Top U900 - $35 USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for prize eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating. Unrated players playing in the U1401 section are only eligible for place prizes (i.e. 1st-2nd). Unrated players are eligible for all prizes in the Open section. Non-rated 1st - $40 2nd - $20 3rd - $10 Schedule: Onsite Registration and Check-In: 9:00am-9:45am Open and U1401 Sections Round 1: 10:00am Round 2: 11:45am Lunch Break Round 3: 2:00pm Round 4: 3:45pm Estimated end: 5:30pm Non-Rated Section *Rounds will start ASAP, generally 15 minutes after the conclusion of the previous round Round 1: 10:00am Round 2: 15 minutes after the end of Round 1 Round 3: 15 minutes after the end of Round 2 Round 4: 15 minutes after the end of Round 3 Estimated end: 1:30pm Players arriving after registration will receive one half-point bye and will be paired in subsequent rounds. Half-point byes may be requested for any round during registration only. Boards and pieces will be provided. Please bring clocks (clocks will be provided for the Non-rated section). Board 1 in the Open Section may be streamed via Facebook Live or Youtube. Please contact tournament organizer if you have any questions. 1700+ USCF rating (1600+ FIDE). See other listing for details. Structure - 3 rounds Swiss-Style. G75 +15. Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion. - One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points. - Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent. Schedule - Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm. - Players should arrive no later than 9:45 am. Registration - Registration fee: $45 - Online registration only. Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. the day of the event. On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion. - Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament - All sections in this tournament have a minimum rating to participate. Under 1400 = 1000 USCF rating minimum Under 1800 = 1300 USCF rating minimum - This event has no age restrictions. - All ratings are assessed based on the published USCF rating supplement for the month the tournament takes place. "Live" or "up-to-date" ratings may be accepted at the director's discretion. - Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section. - Players who sign up but are ineligible to participate, or players who withdraw from the tournament prior to 9:00 am on tournament day, will be provided a credit for a signup for a future tournament or class. Prizes $640 guaranteed in prizes Prizes are paid out via Venmo, Zelle, or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options. U1800 section - 1st place: $160 - 2nd place: $100 - Top U1600: $60 U1400 section - 1st place: $160 - 2nd place: $100 - Top U1200: $60 @45 players (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee. Everyone wins! @50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section @55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section @60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __ rating" prizes for all sections by $15 @65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20. Additional information - The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event. - The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses. No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available. Equipment: Chess sets, notation sheets and pencils will be provided. Please bring your own clock if you can. Prizes : Trophies to top 6 in each section Registration: https://tinyurl.com/FremontGirls2026Reg Registration closes once we hit our maximum capacity of 70! Venue: 2017 Belle View Blvd. Alexandria, VA 22307. The rec center has recently been renovated and features state-of-the-art facilities including a gym, two skating rinks, an indoor pool, and a rock-climbing wall. Organizer: MVP Chess is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Alexandria, Virginia. Our mission is to make chess accessible for everyone and develop growth-minded players. For questions, please email [email protected] . Register Now: MVP Chess K-12 Quads | April 2026 - Organized by MVP Chess | Chess Nut Entry & Donations This tournament is FREE for all US Chess members in grades K–12. An active US Chess membership is required — you can join or renew here . The event is limited to 32 players, so please register in advance to secure your spot and help us plan pairings and sections. We welcome voluntary donations to help cover the cost of room rental, awards, and other tournament-related expenses. All contributions are tax-deductible and may be made online or onsite at the event. Format 3-round quad (final section may be a small Swiss) Time control: G/25; d5 (25 minutes per player, 5-second delay) Rated by US Chess Awards 🏆 Trophies for each quad winner 🎖️ Medals for all other participants 📺 Game Analysis Feature: Select games will be analyzed on the MVP Chess YouTube channel. To be considered, players should submit their scoresheets at the end of the event. Schedule Check-in: 12:45 PM Round 1: 1:00 PM Rounds begin as soon as prior games finish Expected finish: no later than 4:00 PM Rules & Expectations US Chess rules apply Notation optional Chess sets and clocks provided Parents/guardians should stay on-site during the event Please show respect for opponents, staff, and the venue Media Policy MVP Chess may take photos or short video clips for educational and promotional purposes. Names will not be published without consent. If you prefer not to be photographed, simply let us or the photographer know. Gilligan's Bar and Grill Monday, April 27, 2026 Event Overview Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.) Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level. Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad. We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings. Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads. Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament. FM+ are free before late fee deadline. Please email [email protected] for entry under these conditions. How do I get a FIDE ID? Play in one of our FIDE tournaments and fill the registration form and we’ll take care of it for you. Alternatively, you can contact USCF and request an ID as well. USCF membership required in all sections. This tournament is an Iowa State Chess Association Grand Prix points Mini-Qualifier in the Open section. Open: $35 online in advance or $40 cash-only in-person same day Reserve: $25 online in advance or $30 cash-only in-person same day Beginner/Youth: $20 online in advance or $25 cash-only in-person same day Register online at https://www.kingregistration.com/event/QuadCityCincoDeMayo2026 Sections & Time Controls: Open: 4-Round Swiss, G/65, d5 Reserve (under 1400): 4-Round Swiss, G/60, d5 Beginner/Youth (under 800): 4-Round Swiss, G/20, d0 ♟️♟️♟️ Open & Reserve Section Rounds: 1st round: 10:00am Lunch Break - Pizza and Drinks included with registration fee 2nd round: 1:30pm 3rd round: 4:00pm 4th round: 6:30pm *Rounds may start earlier if prior round has been completed and if all players are in agreement. Beginner/Youth Section Rounds: 1st round: 10:00am and then Rounds 2-4 ASAP there after with Lunch break approximately between 3rd & 4th rounds ♟️♟️♟️ Prizes: Open Section: 1st Place: $150 ; 2nd Place: $100 ; 3rd Place: $75 ; 4th Place: $50 Reserve Section (under 1400): 1st Place: $100 ; 2nd Place: $75 ; 3rd Place: $50 Beginner/Youth Section (under 800): Trophies for 1st - 5th Place ; 6th - 20th Place will receive participation medals. ♟️♟️♟️ Additional info: US Chess Federation (USCF) membership required. On Site Registration Available. $3 off for adults, young adults and students if you register through our affiliation. Parents/Guardians of young chess players are responsible for their children. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or coffee in waiting area while games are in progress. Boards and clocks will ONLY be provided for the Beginner/Youth section games. Open and Reserve section players must bring their own regulated clock and board (dimensions listed below). Notation of moves on scoresheet is mandatory for Open and Reserve sections games. Scoresheets will be provided. No electronic scoresheets allowed. By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well. ♟️♟️♟️ For questions: Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890 ♟️♟️♟️ Tournament Directors: Eric Vigil & Mariela Treviño ♟️♟️♟️ Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette: Scoresheets: Notation of moves in Open and Reserve sections is required. Players must record moves in algebraic notation, typically writing the move after executing it on the board. Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute. Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible. One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock. Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically. Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent). Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand. "J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it. Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square. No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play. Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be courteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen. Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe. Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent. USCF Board Regulations & Features: Square Size: 2.25 inches is standard, though 2 to 2.5 inches is permissible. Overall Size: 20" x 20" or 22" x 22" (approx. 50-55 cm). Material: Usually flexible vinyl, often featuring algebraic notation on all sides. Proportion Requirement: The King's base diameter should occupy roughly 75% to 80% of the square size. Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section. ♟️♟️♟️ Western Illinois Chess Club Mission Statement: To strengthen our community by bringing people together through providing opportunities for chess education, fostering respect, collaboration, and mutual growth. At-Risk-Youth Seniors Women menu arrow_back SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15) Sunday, May 3, 2026 Event Overview REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments! All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome. Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance. The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration. For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year). Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#). However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional. If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy! [If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.] Here are the details: Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door). Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm. 4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system. A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost. Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes. Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds. G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move. USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration. This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play. Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating. Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess. Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under). Want your child to "play up?" Just email Mike at [email protected] . Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections. There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month). Notation is required in the premiere sections. The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section. Casual Tournament: Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time. The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout. It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number). There will be four rounds. There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners! Other details: Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director. Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months). An outside playground is available. Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria. There is a guest WiFi network with password August27. The site is wheelchair accessible. Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function. Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available. Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids. If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough. Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections. In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen). Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify). Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament! Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link). Questions? Email Mike at [email protected] . We hope to see you there! REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events Address: 6131 N Michigan Rd. Tournament Features We pair rounds as early as possible and start rounds on time You have time to get ready and don't have to waste your time waiting for the round to start Players like the way we run our events Survey results from a previous Maryland Open 30 second increment time control in the top six sections → No more clock smashing scrambles at the end of the game. Score-based prizes → See the advantages below. Additional 1st place prizes to clear first when there is no 5-0 player in the section, added to your score prize → More prize money >Sets and boards, and clocks provided in ALL sections → All you need to do is show up. Minimum ratings to play in the top six sections → Less mismatch games. Free Sunday morning Continental breakfast → Relax, have some coffee and a danish before you start your game. Texting or emailing of pairings to your cell phone available → No rush at the pairing chart before the round $149/ per night room rate → Relax and stay at the tournament hotel. $5 EF discount if staying at hotel Reserve a room Hotel next to DC Metro stop → Take the Metro directly to the tournament. Shorter time controls in lower sections → Less waiting around between rounds. Prizes This tournament will pay prizes based solely on your final score. All the prizes are guaranteed. If the total pay out in the Open section is less than $1500, extra money will be added to the pay out of the top score group to bring the total to $1500. Advantages over place-based scoring Less Waiting Your score determines your prize. Once you finish your last game, you can receive a check. Less Uncertainty Your prize does not get lowered if others tie with you. For example, if there are two 5-0 players, both receive the full amount for 5-0. Less short draws The total payout is always higher when games are decisive. Please complete all your Quad games. WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad. ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!! benefit and encourage both new and experienced players. MONTHLY SPECIAL PROMOTIONS & ANNOUNCEMENTS: Always FREE registration for players with current USCF rating over 2000! Entry fee deducted from winnings. SPECIAL AWARD: TBA! 2025-2026 SEASON SPECIAL PROJECTS, CONTESTS & SPECIAL RECOGNITIONS: 2025-2026 Brilliancy Award - The player with the most brilliant move this season will receive an award at the May Open! 2025-2026 Texas Chess Association Region I Recognition Program (Details are to be determined) - Awards will be presented at the May Open! DATE: Saturday, May 9, 2026 LOCATION: Mad Hatter's House of Games; 1507 Texas Ave., Lubbock, TX 79401 START TIME: Round 1 begins at 11 AM (Players registered in advance online arrive to pay and check-in before 10:45; Players registering onsite arrive before 10:30am) END TIME: Most sections will finish at approximately 5:30 PM. The Novice Sections will finish at approximately 4:30 PM if players use full time allowed, but usually end earlier. Section awards will be presented shortly after all players in a section have completed their final round. Lower sections typically wrap up earlier than higher sections. COST: FREE REGISTRATION for players with current USCF rating over 2000 (entry fee deducted from winnings); $16/player for Early (Online at https://forms.gle/FpBLjQYmqnBAkN6F9 ) or $21/player for Late (On-site) registration. Payment options include PayPal at the time of online registration or cash on-site at the door. ***There is a $1 cash payment discount, bringing cash payments down to $15 for early registration or $20 for onsite registration.*** REGISTRATION DEADLINES: Early (Online at https://forms.gle/FpBLjQYmqnBAkN6F9 ) pre-registrations are due by 6 PM Friday, May 8, 2026. Late (On-site) registrations must be done between 10:00 and 10:30 AM on Saturday, May 9, 2026. TOURNAMENT DETAILS: Tournament Director: Robert Moore, Region I Director – Texas Chess Association USCF Rated Event: Current USCF membership required - PLEASE update your membership prior to tournament day. Contact us if you need help registering or renewing your USCF membership. Schedule: This is a swiss style tournament; See below for number of rounds and time controls for each section. Pairings will be posted 5 minutes after the last game in the previous round ends, and the new round will begin 10 minutes after the previous round is complete. This effectively adds a 10-minute break for players who are the last to finish a round. Round 1 begins promptly at 11 AM. Equipment: Chess sets and notation supplies will be provided. Some chess clocks will be available, but please bring your own clock if you have one . Five sections as follows: Open Championship - Must be rated above 1300. If fewer than 8 players are above 1300, highest rated players below 1300 will be used to ensure at least 8 players in the section; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5 Reserve A (U1300) - Rating between 950 and 1300 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5 Reserve B (U1000) - Rating between 750 and 1000 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5 Novice A (U800) - Rating between 350 and 800 and unrated scholastic players; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5 Novice B (U400) - Rating under 400 and unrated players 5th grade or below; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5 EXCEPTIONS FOR PROVISIONALLY RATED PLAYERS : Adult players with provisional ratings below 750 may choose to play up into a Reserve section, but they may also register for the novice section that matches their provisional rating. Scholastic players with provisional ratings may be placed in an appropriate section by the tournament director. NOTE ABOUT PLAYERS' SECTION PLACEMENT: At the TD's discretion, sections may be added, deleted, or combined. A player near the rating cut-off may be moved to maintain an even number of players in as many sections as possible. Also, at the TD's discretion, section rating ranges may be revised onsite based on natural breaks in rating distributions, which could increase the number of players in the Open Championship section to more than 8. RATING DETERMINATION: USCF ratings as of May 4 will be used to determine section eligibility for this event. Prizes: Cash prizes for Open Championship and Reserve Sections: Cash prize guarantees are based on 50 registered players . The total guaranteed prize fund for 50 players is $350. The available cash prize fund will be increased or decreased based on registration variance from 50 players. At 100 players, the prize fund will grow to $1000! If there are fewer than 50 players, prizes may be given for fewer than 3 places in each section. Ties will follow USCF rules for splitting cash prizes. Trophies & medals for Novice sections: Trophies will be awarded to the top three finishers in each Novice section. Medals will be awarded to players who tie for third but do not receive a trophy. Standard tie breaks will be used. PHOTOGRAPHY: Photos may be taken during the tournament and awards ceremony. These images may be shared with Texas Chess Association, news outlets, or other interested groups or individuals. Images may be used for promotion of subsequent chess events. CONTACT: Completing the registration form linked below should generate an email to the address used to complete the form. Prior to the tournament, another email communication will be sent with a link to check tournament registration details. This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address ! Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 ) Tournament Director International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 ) Tournament Purpose This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026 and is dedicated to Memorial Day (May 25, 2026) Date & Time Round 1 starts on May 10, 2026, at 10:00 AM . Venue Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009. Time Control G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move). Format 6-round Swiss system. Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions). Ratings This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official May 2026 USCF ratings will be used. Byes Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration. No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes . A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round. Entry Fee $60 – Until April 10, 2026, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first. $80 – Until May 1, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first. $100 – Until May 10, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled. Cancellation & Refund Policy A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by May 6, 2026, at 12:00 AM (midnight) . No refunds will be issued after this deadline. Withdrawal Policy Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw. Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC. Number of Entries Maximum of 64 participants. Eligibility Open to all players with active USCF membership . Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1. Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee. Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes. Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie . Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before May 17, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize. Tiebreaks Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods : Solkoff Modified Median Cumulative If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner. Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) . No electronic devices (phones, smartwatches, etc.) are allowed unless explicitly permitted by the arbiter for medical reasons . A designated storage box will be provided for electronic devices. Photography & Video Recording By registering, players consent to being photographed and recorded by the Tournament Director and their associates for promotional purposes. Equipment & Notation Rules Chess sets, clocks, scoresheets, and pens will be provided by the organizer. Notation is mandatory unless a player has less than 5 minutes remaining on their clock. Players may keep a yellow scoresheet copy and a pen . However, players are encouraged to bring an extra pen , as available pens may be limited . This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address ! PETERSBURG EXTRA QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT G60; d5. Saint Petersburg Chess Club Saturday, May 23, 2026 Event Overview There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games. WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list. The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad. ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!! chessacademy.com/tournaments ! This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address ! Sunday, May 31, 2026 Event Overview 2026 Virginia Senior & Adults Open AND ADULTS-ONLY BLITZ!! at the Country Inn & Suites by Radisson 10358 Patriot Hwy, Fredericksburg, VA Friday - Sunday, May 29 – 31, 2026 Organized by the Virginia Chess Federation WHAT : The 2026 Virginia Senior and Adults Open Chess Championship, with Saturday night Adults-only Blitz. WHEN : Friday through Sunday, May 29th – 31st, 2026. Round 1 is at 7 PM on Friday , May 29th. WHERE : Country Inn & Suites by Radisson, 10358 Patriot Hwy, Fredericksburg, VA - Hotel rate is $99 per night, plus taxes if reserved by Wednesday, May 27th, 2026. Follow the hotel reservation instructions on the Virginia Chess Federation home page, www.vachess.org . MAIN TOURNAMENT FORMAT : The main event consists of two sections of play using the Swiss System for pairings: - Senior Section : Rated by FIDE and US Chess , observing FIDE Rules. Top Virginia player in this section is eligible to represent Virginia at the 2026 John T. Irwin National Tournament of State Senior Champions to be held in Grand Rapids, MI, during the annual U.S. Open Chess Championships. Players must be at least 50 years old as of August 1, 2026 . We use this date because that is the start date of the Irwin Invitational Tournament. - Under 50 Section : US Chess rated , US Chess rules. For players who are 21 to 49 years old as of August 1, 2026. - 5 rounds , Swiss System. This is not an elimination event! - The Time Control for all 5 rounds is Game-90 with 30 seconds of increment for each move. This time control requires all players to take chess notation for the entire game. - There is a 1-hour “no show/forfeit” rul e in effect. A player who is more than 60 minutes late for the announced start time of any round shall be forfeited for that round. ADULTS-ONLY BLITZ : Four (4) Double-rounds at a time control of Game 5, Delay 2. Play is in two Sections: Open and Under 1500 . All games will be US Chess rated. PLAYER ELIGIBILITY : - Residency Requirements : There are no Virginia residency requirements. This tournament is open to all players who are at least 21 years old as of August 1, 2026 ; no exceptions. - All players must be current members of the US Chess Federation. Virginia-based players must be current members of the Virginia Chess Federation (VCF). You can join US Chess and/or Virginia Chess at www.vachess.org by selecting the appropriate membership option on our Home Page. OPTIONAL BYE REQUESTS : - One half-point Bye is allowed for any round in the Main Tournament (no Bye requests for Blitz). Must be declared by speaking directly with the Chief Arbiter/TD before onsite registration closes at 6:15 pm on Friday May 29th. - Byes requests and changes for Rounds 2 through 5 must be declared at least ONE HOUR before the start of Round 2. Changes after this deadline will be listed as zero-point byes. TOURNAMENT SCHEDULE : Both sections follow the same schedule and time controls. - Friday , May 29th: Round 1 at 7 PM. Pairings will be posted at 6:30 PM. - Saturday , May 30th: Round 2 at 11 AM, Round 3 at 4 PM. Senior and Adult Blitz will be played on Saturday evening at 9 PM (US Chess rated, Game 5, delay 2, enter online or onsite and see the separate TLA for the Blitz event). - Sunday , May 31st: Round 4 at 11 AM, Round 5 at 4 PM - Pairings for Rounds 2-5 will be posted ONE HOUR before the start of the next round. “Tentative Pairings” for the Saturday morning and Sunday morning rounds (Rounds 2 and 4) will be posted the evening prior, but these tentative pairings will be subject to change. PRIZES : GUARANTEED $4,500 prize fund based on 80 paid players . 1st to 3rd place prize amounts are guaranteed in both sections. - Senior Section : + 1st to 3rd Places: $650, $450, $300. Plaque to the Champion and the Top Virginia player. + Top Under 2200: $200 + Plaque + Top Under 1800: $165 + Plaque + Top Under 1400 / Unrated: $145 + Plaque + Top Super Senior (Age 65+): $130 + Plaque - Under 50 Section : + 1st to 3rd Places: $650, $450, $300. Plaque for 1st Place. + Top Under 2000: $200 + Trophy + Top Under 1700: $165 + Trophy + Top Under 1400: $145 + Trophy + Top Under 1000: $130 + Trophy + Top Unrated: $100 + Trophy - Both Sections: + $75 for the Top Upsets in Rounds 1-2 and Rounds 3-5. + An unrated player winning a place prize is limited to $300. REGISTRATION AND ENTRY FEES : - Main Tournament ONLINE Entry: Click here to register now! + $75 online or US mail by Sunday May 17th. + $95 from Monday May 18th through Sunday May 24th. Note that Saturday, May 23rd is the last day to use the US Mail entry option. + $105 starting Monday May 25th and at the tournament site. Cash, checks, credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay accepted onsite. - Main Tournament ONSITE Entry: Friday, May 29th from 3-6:15 PM. Registration also will be open on Saturday from 8-10 AM for players who want to enter the tournament for Round 2. - Optional Adults-only Blitz : $25 in advance, $30 onsite at the tournament. We will pay 90% of the Blitz entry fees we receive by section. (For example, if we have 15 entries in the Blitz Open Section, the minimum prize pool will have $338 in cash awards for that section.) - Entry by US Mail: + Send to Mike Hoffpauir, ATTN: VA Sr./U50 Open, 405 Hounds Chase, Yorktown, VA 23693. + Print and send us the “mail-in entry form” accessible through the VA Chess Federation ( www.vachess.org ) or include the following information with your mail-in entry: Section, US Chess ID, Bye Requests, mailing address, email address, and phone number. Also be sure to let us know whether you are playing Blitz and provide your Blitz Section! Make your check payable to “VCF” or “VA Chess Federation.” + Your Entry is post-marked by Saturday, May 23rd and includes a check written for the proper amount of your entry fees. + Do not send any US Mail entries after May 23rd. - NOTE: We will retain $10 from entries who withdraw before the start of Round 1. RE-ENTRY : $35 . A player who had a disappointing Round 1 can “re-enter” the tournament for Round 2 and receive a Half-point Bye to replace their Round 1 score. The Round 1 game counts for rating points, but the Round 1 loss is replaced with a Half-point Bye. Re-entry also means that any other half-point bye the player requested for a later round will become 0-point byes unless that player decides to play in that round at the time of re-entering the tournament. PAIRINGS : - The Chief Arbiter/TD will use ratings from the US Chess May 2026 Rating Supplement for pairings and prize awards. The May ’26 Rating Supplement is published by US Chess on or about April 19, 2026. Pairings will be made using the higher of each player’s Over-the-Board (OTB) and Online Regular (slow) ratings from the May Rating Supplement unless the Online rating is “stale” compared to the OTB rating. - Players without a US Chess rating but who have a rating in another system recognized by US Chess (e.g., FIDE, Canada, many foreign countries) will be paired according to the Chief Arbiter/TD’s conversion of their foreign rating. The Chief Arbiter/TD is the final authority for ratings used for each player. - “Unrated” players are not unrated if they acquire a US Chess or FIDE rating by Thursday, May 28th. TOURNAMENT EQUIPMENT : - Chessboards, pieces, and chess clocks will be provided for all games. You may use your own. - Use of Electronic Scoresheets is not allowed in the Senior Section unless the player has the approval of the Chief Arbiter. - Health protocols: Masks are optional, but we will have some on hand for anyone who desires to wear one. We also will have ample hand sanitizer and sanitizing wipes. QUESTIONS? This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience. We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games. Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating. Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy. This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare). Everyone will use a clock! We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player. Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both! All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it. If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!). If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up here Please arrive 15 minutes before games start. Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads. Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament. Questions? Please let us know at Click here to show mail address ! Please complete all your Quad games. WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad. ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!! Time control: Game in 40 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided. Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes. Sections: Open, Under 1700, Under 1200 & Under 700. Contact: Liulia Cardona at [email protected] or (602) 402-4985 Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section. Entry Fee: $30.00 by Wednesday; $35 by Friday; $40 same day. Refund Policy: Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund. A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8.
