Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 ) Tournament Director International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 ) Tournament Purpose This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026. Date & Time Round 1 starts on June 14, 2026, at 10:00 AM . Venue Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009. Time Control G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move). Format 6-round Swiss system. Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions). Ratings This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official June 2026 USCF ratings will be used. Byes Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration. No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes . A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round. Entry Fee $60 – Until May 15, 2026, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first. $80 – Until June 1, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first. $100 – Until June 14, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled. Cancellation & Refund Policy A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by June 11, 2026, at 12:00 AM (midnight) . No refunds will be issued after this deadline. Withdrawal Policy Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw. Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC. Number of Entries Maximum of 64 participants. Eligibility Open to all players with active USCF membership . Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1. Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee. Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund . Tournament Schedule (Estimated Round Start Times) 1st Round – 10:00 AM 2nd Round – 11:25 AM 30-minute break 3rd Round – 1:20 PM 4th Round – 2:45 PM 5th Round – 4:05 PM 6th Round – 5:25 PM Closing Ceremony – 6:45 PM Prize Fund Prize distribution is based on the final number of players in the tournament: < 10 players 1st: $300 + plaque Total prize fund: $300 10–15 players 1st: $400 + plaque 2nd: $100 Total prize fund: $500 16–20 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 Total prize fund: $750 21–25 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 3rd: $150 Total prize fund: $900 26–30 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 3rd: $150 Best U1600: $150 Best U1200: $150 Total prize fund: $1,200 31–35 players 1st: $500 + plaque 2nd: $250 3rd: $150 Best U1600: $150 Best U1200: $150 Best U800: $150 Total prize fund: $1,350 36–40 players 1st: $550 + plaque 2nd: $350 3rd: $150 Best U1600: $150 Best U1400: $150 Best U1200: $150 Best U1000: $150 Best U800: $150 Total prize fund: $1,800 41–45 players 1st: $590 + plaque 2nd: $350 3rd: $210 Best U1600: $200 Best U1400: $200 Best U1200: $150 Best U1000: $150 Best U800: $150 Total prize fund: $2,000 46–50 players 1st: $590 + plaque 2nd: $410 3rd: $300 Best U1600: $200 Best U1400: $200 Best U1200: $200 Best U1000: $200 Best U800: $200 Total prize fund: $2,300 > 50 players 1st: $590 + plaque 2nd: $410 3rd: $300 Best U1600: $300 Best U1400: $300 Best U1200: $300 Best U1000: $300 Best U800: $300 Total prize fund: $2,800 If rating prizes are offered, unrated players are eligible only for prizes in the lowest rating group . This does not affect their eligibility for the overall (main) prizes. Prizes are equally shared in case of a tie . Payments will be sent via Zelle/PayPal before June 21, 2026. Prize-winners must contact the organizer immediately after the final round to confirm their preferred payment method. Additionally, the prize winners are required to participate in the prize ceremony following the tournament. Failure to complete these actions will result in disqualification from receiving the prize. Tiebreaks Tiebreaks will be determined using ChessRoster SwissSys , applying standard USCF tiebreak methods : Solkoff Modified Median Cumulative If players are tied for 1st place and all tiebreaks are equal , a coin toss will determine the winner. Anti-Cheating Measures & Electronic Devices Policy All players are subject to electronic device scanning (“wanding”) . No electronic devices (phones, smartwatches, etc.) are allowed unless explicitly permitted by the arbiter for medical reasons . A designated storage box will be provided for electronic devices. Photography & Video Recording By registering, players consent to being photographed and recorded by the Tournament Director and their associates for promotional purposes. Equipment & Notation Rules Chess sets, clocks, scoresheets, and pens will be provided by the organizer. Notation is mandatory unless a player has less than 5 minutes remaining on their clock. Players may keep a yellow scoresheet copy and a pen . However, players are encouraged to bring an extra pen , as available pens may be limited . Several others are within walking distance. Questions? Contact us at [email protected] . Sunday, June 28, 2026 Event Overview https://castlechess.org/grandprix/ Note “No Spectator” policy! IMPORTANT – due to the FIFA World Cup Games in Atlanta, out-of-town players should make their travel and hotel arrangements soon! $12,000 Guaranteed Prize Fund Dates: June 26-28, 2026 Location: Emory University – Emory Student Center 605 Asbury Circle, Atlanta, GA. Free Parking at Emory is at the Peavine Parking Lot, 29 Eagle Row, Atlanta, GA. Use the covered parking deck – do not park in the outside deck or you will be charged. Allow ~15 minutes to walk from Peavine to the ESC. Format: 5 rounds. Time Control: G/90, inc/10. 2-day schedule, round 1, G/60, inc/10. Sections & Prizes: $12,000 fully guaranteed prize fund in 7 sections. Master (2200+): $1700 – $1000 – $500; top U2400 : $600 – $300. 80 USCF Grand Prix Points . Expert (2000-2199): $1000 – $600 – $400. Class A (1800-1999): $800 – $500 – $300. Class B (1600-1799): $600 – $400 – $300. Class C (1400-1599): $500 – $300 – $200. Class D (1200-1399 or Unrated): $500 – $300 – $200. U1200 (100-1199 or Unrated): $500 – $300 – $200. * Strict 100-point rule used for “playing up” a section – see below. June 2026 US Chess ratings usually used. 100-point Rule: Players rated within 100 points of next section cutoff (June USCF supplement or live rating thereafter) may “play up” a section if they choose to. Example: a player rated 1700 on the June rating list (or live rating thereafter) may play up in Class A if they choose to, but not a player rated 1699. No exceptions – do not register for a section that you are ineligible for by rating. Erroneous registrations will be moved to the correct section. Unrated players may enter the Class D or U1200 sections and are eligible for prizes. Prizes are paid on site on Sunday, June 28 until 5:30pm, or mailed out the week of June 30. For prizes of $600+, you must fill out a W-9 form with your Tax ID # and address. Entry Fee : $125 online by June 23 $140 online after June 23 or on-site (cash only, exact change), at least 45 minutes before game. Free entries: All GMs, IMs, WGMs : Free online entry . No deduction if registered by June 20, otherwise $125 deducted from prize. FMs & WIMs currently rated 2200+, All Players currently rated 2400+ . Free online entry . $125 deducted from prize. Re-entry : $60 online or on-site (cash, exact change). Campers who pay for the tournament at registration should not register separately. Registration: Online registration is strongly recommended! On-site registration (not recommended): 3-day – Friday 5:15-5:30pm. 2-day/Re-Entry: Saturday 8:45-9:00am. Re-enter online or on-site. Cash only (exact change) on-site. All registration & re-entry closes 1 hour before game. Bye request/change deadline: 1 hour before first game. NO CHECK-IN NEEDED if you register online – just show up for your first game. Campers who pay for tournament at registration should not register separately. Schedule: 3-day Schedule (5 rounds): Friday 6:30pm Saturday 1:30pm Saturday 6:00pm Sunday 9:30am Sunday 1:45pm 2-day Schedule (5 rounds): Round 1 – Saturday 10:00am (G/60, inc/10) Merge with 3-day schedule above starting round 2, Saturday 1:30pm. Up to two half-point byes available, commit before first round . All byes requested during the tournament are zero points. Contact: [email protected] – Chief TD Grant Oen Notes: NO SPECTATORS – during active rounds, parents, spectators, and players that have finished their games are not permitted in the playing room or nearby hallways. Only staff and active players may be in the tournament hall and immediate hallways during play. Boards, sets, and clocks are supplied for the tournament only – bring your own for analysis or skittles. Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Tie-Breaks (Year-End): 1. Most 1st-place finishes. 2. Head-to-head results. 3. Most tournaments played. 4. Best December result. TD decisions are final. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8. PERFECT OPPORTUNITY TO MAKE FRIENDS!!!!! https://www.semperprimuschesscamp.com/ Semper Primus Chess Camp is tailored to students entering K-12th grade . All camp Tournaments are Rated . Overview: We are an overnight chess camp focused on allowing campers to play and learn about the game we love. Our goal is to bring campers of varying ages and levels together to foster both chess skills and community. When: General camp length will be from July 12th – July 17th and July 26th – July 29th (Two great options!) Campers will have the option to attend camp for 5 or 3 days for the July 12th-17th camp. Extra day (July 18th) checkout option will be available to campers, as a tournament will be held on July 18th. Where: Millersville University, Pennsylvania Campers have the option to stay in the suites (5th-12th grade), stay in the suites with a parent/guardian (K-4th grade), or commute (K-12th grade). Double Suite and Single Suite accommodations. Itinerary: Campers will have plenty of events to play and compete in. Recreational activities will be provided in addition to chess to allow campers to rest their minds and relax. Two daily rated tournaments. Evening events may include sports, non-chess activities, Blitz, or quick chess. Freedom of choice is a standard, with camp counselors staying on site 24 hours a day. Formats include Swiss, Quads, and Blitz. Master Instruction ​o We will have masters that provide analysis on your games. ​o Daily group lessons on tactics, strategy, openings, and endgames. o Instruction will be an elective rather than a mandated event. Note To Parents: First, I’d like to thank you for considering our Chess Camp. As a father of four I know how important it is to provide them with opportunities to grow. I grew up with 2 brothers and 2 sisters and it was my oldest brother who was born with cerebral palsy that introduced me and taught me the game of chess. I decided to start up this camp because in my own search for a chess camp had a hard time finding one that allowed for campers to have a full overnight experience, let alone on a college campus. I wanted to have an overnight camp as I find in my dealings with this younger generation that they could use some more time around their peers and making new friends. I expect to continue to improve the instruction and development of these young minds by bringing in quality Masters who can better their game. I am pleased to already have some talented Masters for or 2024 staff. All chess tournaments are run by a USCF Tournament Director. Our staff includes a Director, an Assistant Director, a Tournament Director, 3-4 Masters and camp counselors. We typically have a 1/10 ratio of counselors and campers in the suites. Campers entering 5th through 12th grade may stay in the dorms on their own, while K-4th graders must have a parent/guardian accompanying them. We are equipped to host parents that may want to stay in the area for the week if you don’t mind a suite. Options for 5 night or 3 night stays are available, along with a commuting option. The added day on the registration was designed for parents that don’t want to or can’t pick up their child on Friday but would prefer a Saturday pick up. If you have any questions, please feel free to contact me directly. Brian D. Smith Director 717 984-8011 Click here to show mail address Address: 1 S. Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Tie-Breaks (Year-End): 1. Most 1st-place finishes. 2. Head-to-head results. 3. Most tournaments played. 4. Best December result. TD decisions are final. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8. NEW OPTION for returning players. EMAIL or TEXT MESSAGE us to pre-register and enter the tournament: Email admin@chessearth: 1.) First & Last Name 2.) USCF ID 3.) Section you are playing in and 4.) Pay $45 at the Tournament Site On-Site Entry Fee $50; On-Site Registration – By 9:30am Saturday morning deadline - 10am First Round. On-Site Registration – Ends at 9:30am Saturday morning. 10am First Round. Credit Cards, PayPal, Venmo, CashApp, Zelle, Apple Pay accepted on site Tournament Address: Wyoming Baptist Church, 170 Burns Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45215 4-Round Swiss Tournament Time Control: G/45 +5; Each player receives 45 minutes with a +5-second increment. A Tornado is a one-day tournament where you play four games. Cash Prizes and Awards are given at the end of the tournament based on your final score. Round Start Times: Round #1: 10:00am Round #2: 12:30pm Round #3: 2:30pm Round #4: 4:30pm Choose a Section To Play In: Open Section - Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100 Under 1600 Section Under 1000 Section Award Winning Chili. Good Food; Hot Meals Chess Equipment and Merch available to purchase USCF Rated Tournament. Join/Renew USCF on-site. Purchase a New Membership at Registration. 1/2 Point Bye is available if notified before Round 2. Prizes Fund based on 70 players. We provide all the Chess Clocks & Chess Sets Open Section: **NEW** Rating must be 1600 or above to play in the Open Section. Or a player can pay $30 to “play up” into the Open Section. 1st – $200 2nd – $150 Top Under 2001 – $100 Top Under 1801 – $100 Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100 Master Bounty Prize: Win your game against the #1 Master in the tournament and win $100. If you draw the Master, win $50. If the Master wins all the games, then he/she wins the $100. Under 1600 Section: The heart of the tournament 1st – $200 2nd – $150 $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. Under 1000 Section : Rating must be lower than 1001. Great for beginners and 1st time tournament players. 1st – $200 2nd – $150 $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. PERFECT OPPORTUNITY TO MAKE FRIENDS!!!!! https://www.semperprimuschesscamp.com/ Semper Primus Chess Camp is tailored to students entering K-12th grade . All camp Tournaments are Rated . Overview: We are an overnight chess camp focused on allowing campers to play and learn about the game we love. Our goal is to bring campers of varying ages and levels together to foster both chess skills and community. When: General camp length will be from July 12th – July 17th and July 26th – July 29th (Two great options!) Campers will have the option to attend camp for 5 or 3 days for the July 12th-17th camp. Extra day (July 18th) checkout option will be available to campers, as a tournament will be held on July 18th. Where: Millersville University, Pennsylvania Campers have the option to stay in the suites (5th-12th grade), stay in the suites with a parent/guardian (K-4th grade), or commute (K-12th grade). Double Suite and Single Suite accommodations. Itinerary: Campers will have plenty of events to play and compete in. Recreational activities will be provided in addition to chess to allow campers to rest their minds and relax. Two daily rated tournaments. Evening events may include sports, non-chess activities, Blitz, or quick chess. Freedom of choice is a standard, with camp counselors staying on site 24 hours a day. Formats include Swiss, Quads, and Blitz. Master Instruction ​o We will have masters that provide analysis on your games. ​o Daily group lessons on tactics, strategy, openings, and endgames. o Instruction will be an elective rather than a mandated event. Note To Parents: First, I’d like to thank you for considering our Chess Camp. As a father of four I know how important it is to provide them with opportunities to grow. I grew up with 2 brothers and 2 sisters and it was my oldest brother who was born with cerebral palsy that introduced me and taught me the game of chess. I decided to start up this camp because in my own search for a chess camp had a hard time finding one that allowed for campers to have a full overnight experience, let alone on a college campus. I wanted to have an overnight camp as I find in my dealings with this younger generation that they could use some more time around their peers and making new friends. I expect to continue to improve the instruction and development of these young minds by bringing in quality Masters who can better their game. I am pleased to already have some talented Masters for or 2024 staff. All chess tournaments are run by a USCF Tournament Director. Our staff includes a Director, an Assistant Director, a Tournament Director, 3-4 Masters and camp counselors. We typically have a 1/10 ratio of counselors and campers in the suites. Campers entering 5th through 12th grade may stay in the dorms on their own, while K-4th graders must have a parent/guardian accompanying them. We are equipped to host parents that may want to stay in the area for the week if you don’t mind a suite. Options for 5 night or 3 night stays are available, along with a commuting option. The added day on the registration was designed for parents that don’t want to or can’t pick up their child on Friday but would prefer a Saturday pick up. If you have any questions, please feel free to contact me directly. Brian D. Smith Director 717 984-8011 Click here to show mail address Address: 1 S. Guaranteed 10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5 Columbia Chess Club 6169 St. Andrews Rd. Columbia, SC 29212 Register Registration Standard registration is $40 until midnight on the Thursday before the tournament. $50 late registration thereafter. Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players. Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout. Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players . Register Now Pre-Registered Players Format 4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff. Players may use either their live standard rating or live quick rating to play in a higher section. Players may not play in a section lower than permitted by their published standard rating. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess. Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event. Live Standings/Pairings/Boards The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links. Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below. Live Standings Prizes $1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed. Championship (1600+) $400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70 Under 1600 $300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50 Under 1000 $300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50 Schedule Round 1: 10:30 a.m. Round 2: 12:50 p.m. Round 3: 2:40 p.m. Round 4: 4:30 p.m. Byes A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round. The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances. Location Columbia Chess Club 6169 St. Andrews Rd., Ste A Columbia, SC 29212 Questions? Email [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938. Parking The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking. Food The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks. By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament. Many other restaurants are available close by! Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Tie-Breaks (Year-End): 1. Most 1st-place finishes. 2. Head-to-head results. 3. Most tournaments played. 4. Best December result. TD decisions are final. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout. Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players . Register Now Pre-Registered Players Format 4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff. Players may use either their live standard rating or live quick rating to play in a higher section. Players may not play in a section lower than permitted by their published standard rating. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess. Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event. Live Standings/Pairings/Boards The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links. Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Tie-Breaks (Year-End): 1. Most 1st-place finishes. 2. Head-to-head results. 3. Most tournaments played. 4. Best December result. TD decisions are final. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout. Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players . Register Now Pre-Registered Players Format 4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff. Players may use either their live standard rating or live quick rating to play in a higher section. Players may not play in a section lower than permitted by their published standard rating. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess. Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event. Live Standings/Pairings/Boards The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances. Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Tie-Breaks (Year-End): 1. Most 1st-place finishes. 2. Head-to-head results. 3. Most tournaments played. 4. Best December result. TD decisions are final. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8. 10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5 Columbia Chess Club 6169 St. Andrews Rd. Columbia, SC 29212 Register Registration Standard registration is $40 until midnight on the Thursday before the tournament. $50 late registration thereafter. Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players. Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout. Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament? Great! We've put together a guide to help first-time players . Register Now Pre-Registered Players Format 4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff. Players may use either their live standard rating or live quick rating to play in a higher section. Players may not play in a section lower than permitted by their published standard rating. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess. Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event. Live Standings/Pairings/Boards The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com. A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page. See this site's "Live" menu for links. Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below. Live Standings Prizes $1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed. Championship (1600+) $400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70 Under 1600 $300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50 Under 1000 $300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50 Schedule Round 1: 10:30 a.m. Round 2: 12:50 p.m. Round 3: 2:40 p.m. Round 4: 4:30 p.m. Byes A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round. The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances. Location Columbia Chess Club 6169 St. Andrews Rd., Ste A Columbia, SC 29212 Questions? Email [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938. Parking The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking. Food The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks. By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament. Many other restaurants are available close by! Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆 A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required. 4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points. Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section. Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over. Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that. Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event. At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed. Golden Points System: Finish Points 1st Place 20 2nd Place 16 3rd Place 13 4th Place 10 5–6 8 7–10 5 Participation 3 Bonus Points: +3 points — Perfect score (4/4). +2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months. Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions. Tie-Breaks (Year-End): 1. Most 1st-place finishes. 2. Head-to-head results. 3. Most tournaments played. 4. Best December result. TD decisions are final. Address: 18440 N. 7th Street Suite 8. Sunday, November 29, 2026 Event Overview https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/usmasters OVERVIEW The 2026 US Masters is a US Chess National Championship held over Thanksgiving Weekend. The USM is part of the FIDE Circuit and offers GM/IM norms and a $25,000 guaranteed prize fund. The USM is held just after the Fall GM/IM Norm Invitational and runs alongside the NC Open , an open event for all players. New this Year: Higher rating minimums for untitled juniors Larger female and senior prizes Adjusted time control from G/90 to G/80, inc/30, allowing for a more relaxed schedule while still being valid for norms, rating, and the FIDE Circuit. WHEN November 25-29, 2026 ​ WHERE Hilton Charlotte University Place 8629 JM Keynes Drive Charlotte, NC 28262 Free Internet, Free Parking ​ $139/Night Booking Link - Book ASAP Click "edit stay" at the top of the booking page to select your exact dates Please email us if the booking link is not showing the correct rate. REGISTRATION Online registration required . Online registration closes November 25, 4:00pm On-site check-in is not necessary for pre-registered players. ELIGIBILITY Players rated or once rated 2200+ USCF or FIDE based on an established rating of 26+ games. Players with the NM, FM, WFM, or higher titles. CFC and other foreign National Masters accepted. CM and WCM titles are not considered. Untitled juniors (born 2007 or after) must be rated 1950+ FIDE and 2100+ USCF at any time between September 1 and November 25; the ratings need not be achieved concurrently. Additional fee applies. No exceptions to eligibility rules. Players who do not qualify for the USM may enter the NC Open . Entry fees are based on status at the time of registration. SPECTATORS Parents, spectators, and other non-players may attend, but during play, are not permitted in any playing halls or nearby hallways and restrooms. May enjoy side events and use the hotel common areas. Anyone may register for the $2,000 Blitz on Saturday. TIME CONTROL G/80; inc/30 The USM has been specifically approved by FIDE to be played at a slightly faster classical time control and still be valid for norms, rating, and the FIDE Circuit. PRIZES $25,000 Guaranteed Prize Fund in 1 Section. 150 US Chess Grand Prix Points $7000 - $3500 - $2000 - $1500 - $1400 - $1200 - $1000 Top U2500 FIDE: $1400 - $700 Top U2350 FIDE: $1200 - $600 Top U2200 FIDE: $1000 Bonus Prizes (can be won in addition to other prizes) $500 + USM trophy and title for clear or playoff winner Top Female: $1000 Top Senior (born 1976 or earlier) : $1000 The USM is counted towards the FIDE Circuit , part of the FIDE Candidates cycle. See regulations . NORMS GM, IM, WGM, WIM norms available Norm “Super Swiss” – normal federation requirement waived FIDE requires at least one Swiss norm (40+ players) to obtain GM/IM/WGM/WIM titles SCHEDULE Registration and bye requests close November 26, 4:00pm Wed, 11/25 Round 1 6:00pm Thu, 11/26 Round 2 10:30am Round 3 4:30pm Fri, 11/27 Round 4 10:30am Round 5 4:30pm Sat, 11/28 Round 6 10:30am Round 7 4:30pm $2000 Blitz 9:00pm Sun, 11/29 Round 8 10:00am Round 9 4:00pm Playoff (if necessary) 8:15pm ​SIDE EVENTS FREE $2000 Blitz Saturday, November 29 Starts at 9:00pm Free Entry for USM Players - register on-site by 8:45pm ENTRY FEES Entry fees are based on status at the time of registration. All GMs, IMs, WGMs: Free Online Entry. No deduction from prize by October 10, otherwise $200 deducted. Titled Player Entry (FMs, WIMs, WFMs, NMs): $339 by November 1, $369 by November 15, $399 after November 15. Untitled Juniors (born 2007 or after) with Peak Ratings Under 2200: Must be rated 1950+ FIDE and 2100+ USCF between September 1 and November 25: $400 more than Titled Player Entry. USM players who have an unsuccessful start may withdraw and join the NC Open for a discounted fee of $100 (only available to U2400 FIDE players who are not receiving conditions). Wednesday, December 23, 2026 Event Overview https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/najr OVERVIEW The 2026 North American Junior (U20) Championships will be held December 18-23. The NA Junior is the official Continental Junior Championship of North America and endorsed by the Confederation for Chess in the Americas. This event offers IM/FM titles and GM/IM norms for medalists, as well as a Blitz Championship side event. The NA Junior is held just before the Winter Classic (same venue) and the Winter Elite Camp (different venue). WHEN December 18-23, 2026 ​ WHERE Hilton Charlotte University Place 8629 JM Keynes Drive Charlotte, NC 28262 Free Internet, Free Parking ​ $139/Night Booking Link - Book ASAP Click "edit stay" at the top of the booking page to select your exact dates Please email us if the booking link is not showing the correct rate. REGISTRATION Online registration required . Online registration closes December 17. Same-day registrations may incur a 0-point bye in round 1 at the Chief Arbiter's discretion. This event is US Chess and FIDE-rated. US Chess membership required for all players. On-site check-in is not necessary for pre-registered players. Official Players - each federation (CAN, MEX, USA) may designate one player as their official representative per section. The gold medalists from the 2025 North American Junior Championships may also register as official players in the same sections. ORs receive free entry (full refund is already paid) if fully registered by November 15. Upon completion of the event, they will also be reimbursed a fee of $200 USD to help with travel expenses. ORs registering after November 15 will be considered regular players and are not eligible for OR conditions. ELIGIBILITY Open to players from Canada, Mexico, and USA who are under 20 years old (19 and younger) as of 1/1/2026. All players must be born on or after 1/1/2006. Players' FIDE federation must show CAN, MEX, or USA. This event is US Chess and FIDE-rated. US Chess membership required for all players. There is no rating or title minimum or maximum. Girls may enter either section - Open U20 or Girls U20. Erroneous registrations will be subject to the refund policy. Register Now Pre-Registered Players Format 4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff. Players may use either their live standard rating or live quick rating to play in a higher section. Players may not play in a section lower than permitted by their published standard rating. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess. Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event. Last Saturday of Month Wyoming Baptist Church Saturday, December 26, 2026 Event Overview Cincinnati Tornado Monthly Tournament Held on the Last Saturday of the Month We provide all clocks & chess sets Advance Entry Fee $45 Online Registration – By Friday 12 midnight deadline Online Registration: https://chessearth.com/tornado-registration/ Advance Registration ends on Friday 12 midnight. NEW OPTION for returning players. EMAIL or TEXT MESSAGE us to pre-register and enter the tournament: Email admin@chessearth: 1.) First & Last Name 2.) USCF ID 3.) Section you are playing in and 4.) Pay $45 at the Tournament Site On-Site Entry Fee $50; On-Site Registration – By 9:30am Saturday morning deadline - 10am First Round. On-Site Registration – Ends at 9:30am Saturday morning. 10am First Round. Credit Cards, PayPal, Venmo, CashApp, Zelle, Apple Pay accepted on site Tournament Address: Wyoming Baptist Church, 170 Burns Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45215 4-Round Swiss Tournament Time Control: G/45 +5; Each player receives 45 minutes with a +5-second increment. A Tornado is a one-day tournament where you play four games. Cash Prizes and Awards are given at the end of the tournament based on your final score. Round Start Times: Round #1: 10:00am Round #2: 12:30pm Round #3: 2:30pm Round #4: 4:30pm Choose a Section To Play In: Open Section - Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100 Under 1600 Section Under 1000 Section Award Winning Chili. Good Food; Hot Meals Chess Equipment and Merch available to purchase USCF Rated Tournament. Join/Renew USCF on-site. Purchase a New Membership at Registration. 1/2 Point Bye is available if notified before Round 2. Prizes Fund based on 70 players. We provide all the Chess Clocks & Chess Sets Open Section: **NEW** Rating must be 1600 or above to play in the Open Section. Or a player can pay $30 to “play up” into the Open Section. 1st – $200 2nd – $150 Top Under 2001 – $100 Top Under 1801 – $100 Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100 Master Bounty Prize: Win your game against the #1 Master in the tournament and win $100. If you draw the Master, win $50. If the Master wins all the games, then he/she wins the $100. Under 1600 Section: The heart of the tournament 1st – $200 2nd – $150 $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. Under 1000 Section : Rating must be lower than 1001. Great for beginners and 1st time tournament players. 1st – $200 2nd – $150 $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. $100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter. Chess Community Gathering Hang Out & Analyze; Play Casual Chess Games in the Skittles room. TVs are in the Skittle rooms Enjoy Good Food Buy Chess Merch Watch the Tournament. Chess Social Life. We are looking for volunteers to help with the clean-up; putting chairs and tables away. Please email us if you can help. Top U1900: $80, Top U1500: $60 US Chess and FIDE blitz rated. US Chess membership required. Oakland University is located in southeastern Michigan between Flint and Detroit. The 1,441-acre campus actually extends into two cities — Auburn Hills and Rochester Hills, between Adams Road and Squirrel Road, just south of Walton Boulevard. Take I-75 to exit 79 and go east on University Drive to the main entrance of campus. Or, take M-59 to the Squirrel Road exit and go north to the main entrance of campus at the corner of University Drive. From OU’s Main Entrance To get to the Oakland Center from the main entrance of campus, drive around the circle drive past the first entrance to Meadow Brook Road until you get to the second entrance to Meadow Brook Road and turn right. The Oakland Center is located on the right side of the road between North and South Foundation Halls. The best place to park is in Parking Lot 1 or 2. Format: Printable Flyer: Printable Flyer: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RMMuXsTyjjbycyCSt_cZ0n-fR5R9hysW/view?usp=sharing High School: 4-SS, 2 Sections - High School Championship: HS Teams (Gr 9-12), High School Reserve: HS Teams (Gr 9-12) U1000 Avg Team Rating Junior High (No HS 9th Grade Teams per MCA Rules): 5-SS, 2 Sections - Junior High Championship: K-9, Junior High Reserve: K-9 U600 Avg Team Rating Average Team Rating Calculator: https://www.michess.org/team-rating-calculator Michigan Chess Association and USCF Memberships Required for ALL Players Event Policies: MCA Scholastic Code of Conduct & Building Policies will be provided via a separate flyer online and via hard copy during the event. By registering for this event, players, parents, and coaches agree to abide by these policies. Any violations of these policies can lead to withdrawal of all teams from the school and ejection from the facility. Teams: - Each team is composed of 3-5 players. A standard team consists of 4 players. A team may compete with 3 players, possibly forfeiting on board 4. Teams of 5 players are also permitted where any 4 of the 5 players can play each round while keeping consistent board order. - The players on a team must be part of the same educational system (“school’) as defined by USCF Scholastic Regulations Sections 5.2, 5.3, or 5.4. https://new.uschess.org/sites/default/files/media/documents/uschess-scholasticregulations_2024-2025.2024.08.05a.pdf - Multiple teams from the same school may be submitted to any section or event. - There is no requirement that the teams be sponsored by the school. A group of friends that meet the team eligibility requirements can register and compete. - Individual players should not register for the event. Contact MCA for assistance forming a team. - For teams that cannot participate due to last minute withdrawals, the remaining players may still participate in the extra rated games. Section Eligibility: MCA Standing Rule 82-01: Ninth grade students playing in an MCA scholastic team tournament must play in the event for the type of school they attend. Examples: (Adopted 01/13/82) 1. If a high school includes grades 9 12, then those ninth graders would play in the High School Tournament. 2. If a junior high school has grades 7 9, then those ninth graders would play in the Junior High School Tournament. Board Order: MCA Standing Rule 84-03: Regarding board order in team tournaments: Rated players should generally be placed in rating order; unrated players may be placed anywhere. This should be done with fairness in mind: The strongest player on each team should play on first board, no matter whether he has a relatively high or low rating or is unrated. The tournament director may, at his discretion, change submitted player placements, after considering evidence from various sources (non-USCF ratings, other coaches, etc.). (Adopted 06/21/84). Average Team Rating: Use our online tool to determine eligibility for Reserve sections: https://www.michess.org/team-rating-calculator Match Games: Individual games are between the players only without the assistance of parents, coaches, and teammates. All questions or concerns, including current match score, should be directed to the TD. Extra Rated Games: Each round, Fourth boards without an opponent and alternates are paired randomly so they can play rated games. These games are optional, and players are not guaranteed a game. Points scored in these matches DO NOT count for individual medals. Equipment: Boards and Pieces are provided for tournament games. Bring your own set for skittles between rounds. Bring Clocks: Games may start without clocks, but games running long will have a clock placed on them with very little time. Notation: Please bring writing utensils. All players must record the moves of their game until one player has less than 5 minutes remaining on the clock. Cell Phones: No Players may have a cell phone in their possession during their game. Spectators: Parents and Coaches may be separated from the playing area once games begin.
